title: God's Got Big Plans for You, Bro
paragraphs: This is the message from Jeremiah, son of Hilkiah. He was from a family of priests living in a town called Anathoth, in the Benjamin area. God started talking to him in the thirteenth year that Josiah, son of Amon, was king of Judah. He kept getting messages during the time Jehoiakim, son of Josiah, was king, and it continued all the way to the fifth month of the eleventh year that Zedekiah, son of Josiah, was king of Judah. That was the year Jerusalem's people were captured and taken away. This is what God said:

"Yo, before you were even a thought in your mom's head, I knew you. Before you were even born, I had huge plans for you. I'm talking prophet-to-the-nations level stuff. That's what I had in mind for you."
But I was like, "Whoa, hold up, God! Look at me. I'm just a kid. I don't know what I'm doing."

God told me, "Don't give me that 'I'm just a kid' excuse. I'll tell you where to go, and you'll go. I'll tell you what to say, and you'll say it. Don't be scared of anyone. I've got your back, for real." That's what God said.

Then God reached out, touched my mouth, and said, "There. I just put my words in your mouth, fresh from the source. See what I did? You've got a big job to do, dealing with nations and governments. This is a huge day for you. Your job is to pull things up, tear them down, take them apart, and demolish them. And then, you'll start over, building and planting new things."
God's message came to me: "What do you see, Jeremiah?" I said, "A walking stick—that's all." And God said, "Good eyes! I'm sticking with you. I'll make every word I give you come true."

God's message came again: "So what do you see now?" I said, "I see a boiling pot, tipped down toward us." Then God told me, "Disaster will pour out of the north on everyone living in this land. Watch for this: I'm calling all the kings out of the north." God's Decree.

"They'll come and set up their headquarters right in front of Jerusalem's gates, all around the city walls, and in all the towns of Judah. I'm going to lay down my judgment on the people of Judah for leaving me. It was a terrible thing to do. They started chasing after other gods, giving them offerings, and worshiping things they made themselves, like carved sticks and painted stones."
"But you, get up and get ready for work. Stand up and say everything I tell you to say. Don't hold back, or I'll have to take you out of the game."

"Now, pay attention while I get you ready. I'm making you as strong as a fortress, as unmovable as a steel pole, and as solid as a concrete wall. You're going to be a one-man army against this whole culture, against the kings and princes of Judah, against the priests and the local leaders. They'll try to fight you, but they won't even leave a scratch. I'll be there for you every step of the way." That's what God said.

title: God's Got Beef With His People
paragraphs: God's message hit me. It went like this:

"Go and shout this all over Jerusalem: 'God's message! I remember how loyal you were when you were young, like our honeymoon phase. You stuck with me through the wilderness, through all the rough patches. Israel was supposed to be my special possession, the best of the best. Anyone who messed with you would regret it big time!' That's God's decree.

Hear God's message, all you people of Jacob and Israel! God is asking: "What did your ancestors find wrong with me that made them drift so far away? They started chasing empty things and became empty themselves. They never bothered to ask, 'Where's the God who got us out of Egypt, who guided us through that gnarly wilderness—a land of deserts and death traps, a place nobody wanted to be?'

I brought you into a paradise, a land full of good things to eat. But you came in and trashed my land, you totally defiled my special place. The priests never asked, 'Where's God?' The religious experts didn't know me. The leaders rebelled against me. The prophets were busy hyping up a fake god, Baal, chasing after worthless idols and silly ideas.

Because of all this, I'm calling you out," says God. "I'm calling out you, your kids, and your grandkids. Just look around. Have you ever seen anything like this? Go check the islands in the west, or the Kedar wilderness in the east. Look closely. Has any nation ever traded its gods for fake ones that aren't even gods? But my people have traded my glory for worthless idols and silly schemes.

Heavens, be shocked by this! Be horrified!" God declares. "My people have messed up twice. First, they abandoned me, the source of fresh, life-giving water. Then, they dug their own wells—broken wells that can't even hold water.

Isn't Israel supposed to be a treasured member of my family? So how did they end up getting torn apart by enemies like lions, left with nothing but ruins? Even the Egyptians from Memphis and Tahpanhes have crushed you. And why did this happen? Because you walked away from your God right when he was leading you down the right path.

And what do you hope to gain by running to Egypt or Assyria? A drink from the Nile or the Euphrates? No, your own evil will punish you. Your disloyalty will have bitter consequences. You need to see how terrible it was to abandon your God," says the Lord, the God of Angel Armies.

"A long time ago, you threw off my guidance. You said, 'I won't follow you!' and went off to worship every false god you could find, like a prostitute. I planted you as a top-quality vine, the best stock available. But look at you now—a tangled, rotten mess. You can scrub yourself with the strongest soap, but the stain of your sin is still there, and I can't even look at you," says the Lord God.

"How can you even say, 'I'm not dirty; I haven't chased after the Baal gods'? Just look at the evidence you left behind in the valley. You're like a restless camel or a wild donkey in heat, desperately sniffing the air for a mate. Who could control you? You're obsessed, always chasing after more.
"Slow down. What's the rush? Why are you wearing yourself out chasing these things? But you say, 'It's no use. I'm addicted to these foreign gods. I can't stop.'

"Just like a thief is ashamed when caught, the people of Israel are ashamed—their kings, officials, priests, and prophets. They say to a piece of wood, 'You are my father,' and to a stone, 'You gave me birth.' They've turned their backs on me. But when trouble hits, they come running, crying, 'Get up and save us!' Well, where are the gods you made for yourselves? Let them save you. You have more gods than you have towns, Judah.
"Why are you complaining to me when you're the ones who rebelled?" God asks. "I tried to discipline your children, but they wouldn't listen. You've killed the prophets I sent to you.

"What a generation you are! Have I been like a desert to you, Israel? A land of darkness? Why do my people say, 'We're on our own now; we're not coming back to you'? Does a young woman forget her jewelry, or a bride her wedding dress? Yet my people have forgotten me for days without end.

"You're so good at chasing after what you want; you could teach a masterclass in evil. Your clothes are stained with the blood of the innocent poor you've crushed. You didn't even catch them doing anything wrong. And yet you say, 'I'm innocent. God's not mad at me.' But I am bringing judgment against you for saying you haven't sinned.

"You change your loyalties so easily. But Egypt will let you down, just like Assyria did. You will walk away from there in shame, because I, the Lord, have rejected those you trust. You won't get any help from them."

title: God's Got Beef: The Cheating Scandal
paragraphs: God's message hit me, and this is what it said:

"Okay, real talk: if a dude's wife just dips and marries some other guy, can he just welcome her back like, 'Hey, what's up?' No way, right? That would be a whole scandal in the country. And lowkey, isn't that exactly what you've done? You've been messing around with every fake god you could find. And now you have the audacity to come back like it's all cool?" That's a direct quote from God.

"Just look around at the hills. Is there a single place you haven't been unfaithful? You've been out there waiting for lover-gods like a hunter waiting for prey. You've been chasing after them like a prostitute looking for customers. That's why the rain stopped. No more showers from the sky! But you're not even bothered. You're so shameless, acting like you did nothing wrong. And then you have the nerve to hit me up like, 'My Father! You were always there for me when I was young. What about now? Are you gonna stay mad forever?' That's your go-to line, but then you just keep on sinning without a break."

During King Josiah's time, God said to me: "You've seen it, right? How two-timing Israel went and worshiped idols on every hill and under every tree, like a total cheater. I really thought that after she got it all out of her system, she'd come back to me. But she never did. And her flaky sister, Judah, saw the whole thing. She saw that I dumped unfaithful Israel and served her divorce papers because she was so morally bankrupt. But that didn't even scare flaky Judah. She went out, bold as ever, and started living the same cheating life. She treated her religion and relationship with me like some cheap hobby, messing around with anyone and anything, completely disrespecting what's sacred and making the whole country stink. And through all this, flaky Judah didn't even give me a real thought, even though she put on a show every now and then." That's God's decree.
Then God told me, "Honestly, two-timing Israel looks way better than flaky Judah. Go and preach this message. Face north toward Israel and say:

"'Come back, you unfaithful Israel. I'm not just waiting to punish you. I'm committed to you out of love. My anger doesn't last forever. Just own up to what you did. Admit you defied your God. Admit you've been hooking up with random foreign gods under the trees and totally ignoring me.'" That's God's decree. "'Come back, you lost kids!'" God's decree. "'I am your true husband. I'll pick you out one by one—one from this city, two from that town—and I'll bring you to Zion. I'll give you good leaders, shepherds who follow my ways, who will lead you with smarts and wisdom.'

"And here's what's gonna happen: You're gonna grow in number and thrive in the land. The time is coming"—God's decree!—"when no one will be talking about, 'Oh, the good old days with the Ark of the Covenant.' It won't even cross their minds to say it. Those so-called 'good old days' of the Ark are over for good.
"Jerusalem itself will be the new Ark—it'll be called 'God's Throne.' All the nations that don't know God will gather there to honor Him, and they won't be stuck in their old, evil habits anymore.
"In that time, the family of Judah will team up with the family of Israel. They'll walk hand-in-hand out of the northern lands and come back to the land I promised to your ancestors.

"I had this whole speech planned for when you came back to me. I was gonna say: 'Awesome! I'll bring you back into the family. I'll give you the best land, a place all the other nations would kill for.' And I imagined you'd call me 'Dear Father!' and would never leave me again. But nope. Like a wife who cheats on her husband, you, the whole family of Israel, have been totally unfaithful to me." God's decree.

You can hear voices coming from the hills, the sad sound of Israel crying, mourning all the wasted years when they never gave their God a single thought. "Come back, you wandering children! I can fix your unfaithfulness!"

"We're here! We're coming back to you. You are our one true God! All that other popular religion was just a cheap fake, with crowds getting tricked into buying the newest trendy gods. We're back! We're back to our true God, the one who saves Israel. That Fraud took everything from us, scammed us out of the inheritance our ancestors left, and ripped off our God-given flocks and kids. We made our bed, and now we have to lie in it, tangled up in the dirty sheets of our own shame. It's all because we sinned against our God, us and our parents before us. From the moment we could walk and talk, we've been rebels, straight-up disobeying the voice of our God."

title: God's ANGER Issues Are Next Level
paragraphs: “Yo, Israel, if you’re serious about coming back to me, you gotta actually come back. Ditch all that gross stuff you’ve been worshiping and stop wandering off. Then, when you say stuff like, ‘As God lives,’ it’ll actually mean something real and right. And all the other nations will get in on the blessing and see something in you worth talking about.”

Here’s another message from God for the people of Judah and Jerusalem: “Get your unplowed fields ready, but don’t plant weeds in them! Seriously, dedicate your lives to God. Soften up those hard hearts, all you people of Judah and Jerusalem. You gotta stop my anger from turning into a wildfire, because once it starts, it’s not going out. Your wicked lifestyle is the fuel for that fire.

“Sound the alarm in Judah, shout it out in Jerusalem! Tell everyone to blow the trumpets all over the country! Yell it out loud: ‘Everyone, group up! Run to the fortified cities for safety!’ Signal a warning to Zion: ‘Hurry, don’t wait!’ A huge disaster is coming from the north, and I’m the one sending it. It’s gonna be devastating. An invader is coming like a lion out of its den, a destroyer of nations. It’s on the move to wreck your land, leave your cities in ruins, and make them ghost towns. So put on black clothes, cry your eyes out, because God’s crazy anger is coming right for us.
“When that happens,” God says, “the king and his officials will totally lose it, the priests will be clueless, and the prophets will be speechless.”
Then I was like, “Oh man, Lord GOD! You totally tricked this people and Jerusalem. You told them, ‘Everything’s gonna be fine,’ right when a sword was at their throats.”

At that time, this is what will be told to this people, to Jerusalem: “A scorching wind is blowing in from the desert, heading for my people. It’s not a gentle breeze for winnowing grain; it’s a full-on gale-force wind that I’ve commanded. I’m about to drop my hurricane-level judgment on them.”

Look at them coming! They look like a huge bank of storm clouds. Their chariots are like a tornado, and their horses are faster than eagles! We’re so doomed! We’re done for! Jerusalem, you gotta wash the evil out of your heart so you can be saved. How much longer are you gonna let those twisted, evil thoughts hang around in your head?

Listen! A messenger is coming from Dan, bringing bad news from the hills of Ephraim! Announce it to the nations, broadcast it to Jerusalem: “Invaders are coming from a distant land, and they’re shouting war cries against the towns of Judah. They’re surrounding the city like guards watching a field, because she rebelled against me,” says the LORD.
“It’s your own lifestyle and your own actions that brought this on you. This is your punishment, and it’s a bitter one. It’s a pain that cuts straight to your heart.”

I’m doubled over in pain, my stomach is in knots. My heart is pounding inside me, I can’t keep quiet. I hear the sound of the trumpet, the battle cry for war. It’s one disaster after another; the whole land is in ruins! My home was destroyed in a second, my tents torn down in an instant. How long do I have to see the war flags and hear the trumpets of danger?
“My people are such idiots! They don’t even know who I am. They’re a bunch of clueless kids, total morons. They’re pros at doing evil, but they have no idea how to do good.”

I looked at the earth, and it was a total mess, completely empty, like before creation. I looked at the sky, and there were no stars. I looked at the mountains, and they were shaking, and all the hills were swaying back and forth. I looked, and there was no one left, not a single person. All the birds in the sky were gone. I looked, and the fertile land had become a desert. All the towns were destroyed. And it was all because of the LORD, because of his burning anger.

Yes, this is what the LORD says: “The whole land will be destroyed, but I won’t completely wipe it out. The earth will be in mourning, and the sky will be dark, because I have spoken, and I’m not taking it back. I’ve made my decision, and I’m not changing my mind.”

At the sound of the horsemen and archers, everyone is running for their lives. They’re hiding in the thickets and climbing up into the rocky cliffs. All the towns are abandoned; not a single person is left.

And you, what do you think you’re doing? Why are you putting on your fancy red dress and all your gold jewelry? Why are you putting on so much makeup? You’re making yourself beautiful for nothing. Your lovers despise you; they want to kill you. I hear a cry like a woman in labor, a scream like someone giving birth to her first child. It’s the cry of Daughter Zion, gasping for breath, stretching out her hands and saying, “Help me! I’m about to die! The murderers are all around me!”

title: God's Looking for ONE Good Person...Can He Find One?
paragraphs: Yo, go patrol the streets of Jerusalem. Look around, take notes. Search the market squares. See if you can find just one person, a single soul, who does what's right and tries to live a true life. I want to forgive that person. That's God's decree. But if all they do is say, 'As sure as God lives...' they're nothing but a bunch of liars.

But you, God, you have an eye for truth, don't you? You hit them hard, but it didn't even faze them. You disciplined them, but they refused to be corrected. They're hardheaded, harder than a rock; they wouldn't change. Then I said to myself, 'Well, these are just poor people. They don't know any better. They were never taught anything about God. They never went to prayer meetings. I'll go find some people from the best families. I'll talk to them. They'll know what's going on, the way God works. They'll know the score.' But they were no better! They were all rebels, off doing their own thing. The invaders are ready to pounce and kill, like a mountain lion, a wilderness wolf, or panthers on the prowl. The streets aren't safe anymore. And why? Because the people's sins are piled sky-high; their betrayals are past counting.

Why should I even bother with you any longer? Your children wander off, leaving me, taking up with gods that aren't even gods. I satisfied their deepest needs, and then they went off with the 'sacred' unfaithful ones, left me for orgies in sex shrines! A bunch of well-groomed, lusty stallions, each one pawing and snorting for his neighbor's wife. Do you think I'm going to stand around and do nothing? That's God's decree. Don't you think I'll take serious measures against a people like this?

Go down the rows of vineyards and rip out the vines, but not all of them. Leave a few. Prune back those vines! That growth didn't come from God! They've betrayed me over and over again, both Judah and Israel. That's God's decree.

They've spread lies about God. They've said, 'There's nothing to him. Nothing bad will happen to us, neither famine nor war will come our way. The prophets are all windbags. They speak nothing but nonsense.'
Therefore, this is what God said to me, God-of-the-Angel-Armies:
Because they have talked this way, they are going to eat those words. Watch now! I'm putting my words as fire in your mouth. And the people are a pile of kindling ready to go up in flames.

Attention! I'm bringing a far-off nation against you, O house of Israel. That's God's decree. A solid nation, an ancient nation, a nation that speaks another language. You won't understand a word they say. When they aim their arrows, you're as good as dead. They're a nation of real fighters! They'll clean you out of house and home, rob you of crops and children alike. They'll feast on your sheep and cattle, strip your vines and fig trees. And the fortresses that made you feel so safe—leveled with a stroke of the sword!

Even then, as bad as it will be—that's God's decree!—it will not be the end of the world for you. And when people ask, 'Why did our God do all this to us?' you must say to them, 'This is back on you. Just as you left me and served foreign gods in your own country, so now you must serve foreigners in their own country.'

Tell the house of Jacob this, put out this bulletin in Judah: Listen to this, you scatterbrains, airheads, with eyes that see but don't really look, and ears that hear but don't really listen. Why don't you honor me? Why aren't you in awe before me? Yes, me, who made the shorelines to contain the ocean waters. I drew a line in the sand that cannot be crossed. Waves roll in but cannot get through; breakers crash but that's the end of them. But this people—what a people! Uncontrollable, untamable runaways. It never occurs to them to say, 'How can we honor our God with our lives, the God who gives rain in both spring and autumn and maintains the rhythm of the seasons, who sets aside time each year for harvest and keeps everything running smoothly for us?' Of course you don't! Your bad behavior blinds you to all this. Your sins keep my blessings at a distance.

My people are infiltrated by wicked men, unscrupulous men on the hunt. They set traps for the unsuspecting. Their victims are innocent men and women. Their houses are stuffed with ill-gotten gain, like a hunter's bag full of birds. Pretentious and powerful and rich, hugely obese, oily with rolls of fat. Worse, they have no conscience. Right and wrong mean nothing to them. They stand for nothing, stand up for no one, throw orphans to the wolves, exploit the poor. Do you think I'll stand by and do nothing about this? That's God's decree. Don't you think I'll take serious measures against a people like this?

Unspeakable! Sickening! What's happened in this country? Prophets preach lies and priests hire on as their assistants. And my people love it. They eat it up! But what will you do when it's all over? Can you live with your lying prophets and wicked priests? 'Cause you never seem to learn!

title: Jerusalem Is SO Canceled
paragraphs: “Yo, people of Benjamin, you gotta bounce! Get out of Jerusalem, like, right now! Sound the alarm in Tekoa, send up smoke signals from Beth Hakkerem. Something terrible is coming from the north, it's gonna be a total nightmare. I thought my girl Zion was like a beautiful, peaceful field. But now, these enemy ‘shepherds’ have found her and are bringing in their whole crew of soldiers. They’ve set up camp all around her, deciding who gets to ‘graze’ where. And then they’re like, ‘Let’s get ready to fight! Attack! We’ll hit ‘em at noon! Oh wait, it’s getting late? The sun’s going down? The evening shadows are getting long? Whatever, let’s go! We’ll attack tonight and wreck their defenses completely.’”
God, the commander of heavenly armies, gave the orders:

“Chop down their trees. Build a ramp to attack Jerusalem, a city that’s just full of cruelty and bursting with violence. You know how a well is always full of water? That’s how much evil is in her, nonstop. All you hear in the streets are cries of ‘Violence! Assault!’ There are wounded and moaning people everywhere. You’re in some serious trouble, Jerusalem. You’ve pushed me to my absolute limit. You’re about to get totally wiped out and turned into a ghost town.”
More orders from God, the commander of heavenly armies:
“It’s over. Time to harvest the grapes for judgment. Save what’s left of Israel. Go back over the vines and pick them clean, every single grape.

“I have something to say, but is anyone even listening? I’m trying to warn you, but will anyone pay attention? It’s useless! Their ears are basically clogged. They’re deaf and blind to it all. It’s hopeless! They’ve totally tuned God out. They don’t want to hear a thing from me. But I’m so full of God’s anger, I can’t hold it in anymore.

“So just let it all out on the kids in the streets. Unleash it on the groups of young people. Because nobody is safe: husbands and wives will be taken, the elderly and those about to die. Their houses will be given away—everything they own, even their families—when I give the signal against everyone living in this country.” This is God’s official statement.

“Everyone is just chasing money, from the least important person to the most important. Prophets and priests, all of them, are twisting words and faking the truth. My people are completely broken—shattered!—and they’re just putting on little Band-Aids, saying, ‘It’s cool, you’ll be fine.’ But things are NOT fine! You think they’re embarrassed about all this messed-up stuff? Nah, they have zero shame. They don’t even know how to blush. There’s no hope for them. They’ve hit rock bottom and they’re not getting back up. As far as I’m concerned, they’re done.” God has said it.
God’s message, again:

“Go stand at the crossroads and look around. Ask for the old path, the one that’s been tested and is true. Then take it. Find the right way for your souls. But they said, ‘No way. We’re not going that way.’ I even gave them watchmen to warn them, to sound the alarm. But the people said, ‘That’s a false alarm. It’s not for us.’ So now I’m calling all the nations as witnesses: ‘Watch, you witnesses, what happens to them!’ And, ‘Listen up, Earth! Don’t miss this news.’ I’m bringing a disaster on these people, the direct result of the games they’ve been playing with me. They’ve ignored everything I’ve said and had nothing but disrespect for my teaching. Why would I want your incense from Sheba, or your fancy spices from far away? Your burnt offerings mean nothing to me. Your religious ceremonies are pointless.”
So listen up. Here’s God’s final word on your lifestyle:
“Watch out! I’m putting up roadblocks and obstacles on the path you’re on. They’ll make you trip and fall, parents and kids, neighbors and friends—and that’ll be the end of all of you.”
And listen to this verdict from God:

“Look out! An army is coming from the north, a huge force is on its way from a distant land: They’re heavily armed, cruel, and have no mercy. They sound like a roaring sea storm—tramp, tramp, tramp—riding hard on their war horses, in battle formation, coming right for you, dear Daughter Zion!”

We heard the news, and we just went limp. We’re paralyzed with fear. Terror has us by the throat. Don’t even think about going outside! Don’t leave your house! Death is hunting you. There’s danger everywhere!

“Dear Daughter Zion: Put on black clothes. Cover your face with ashes. Cry your eyes out, like you’re mourning for your only child. The countdown has started... six, five, four, three... The Terror is here!”
God gave me this job:

“I’ve made you an examiner for my people, to check out and evaluate their lives. They’re a stubborn, hard-headed crew, totally corrupt, every last one of them. The refining fires are turned up super hot, but the metal just stays a useless lump. It’s pointless to keep trying. You can’t get the evil out of them. People will give up and just call them ‘scrap metal,’ thrown on the scrap heap by me, their God.”

title: Stop Faking It: God's Calling You Out
paragraphs: A message from God came to Jeremiah, and it was a big one. He had to go stand right at the entrance of God's Temple and just let it rip.
He was told to say, 'Yo, listen up, all you people from Judah coming here to worship. The God of Angel Armies, the God of Israel, is laying it all out for you:

'Straight up, you need to fix your lives—how you're living, what you're doing. If you do that, I can actually hang out with you here. But don't even for a second fall for the lie that everyone's repeating: "This is God's Temple, God's Temple, God's Temple!" That's total garbage. The only way this works is if you actually clean up your act. Like, a full-on spring cleaning of your lives and how you treat other people. Stop taking advantage of immigrants, orphans, and widows. Stop letting innocent people get hurt right here, and for real, stop wrecking your own souls by using my Temple as a cover while you're off chasing other gods. Only then will I actually move into your neighborhood. Only then can this land I gave your ancestors be my forever home, my Temple.

'Seriously, get a clue! Your leaders are feeding you a bunch of lies, and you're just eating them up. Use your brains! Do you really think you can go around stealing, murdering, sleeping with your neighbors' partners, lying 24/7, worshipping fake local gods, and collecting every new religious trend out there—and then just stroll into my Temple, the one set aside for me, and say, "We're good!"? Like the building itself gives you a free pass to keep doing all this messed-up stuff? You think you can turn my house into a hideout for criminals? Yeah, right. I have eyes. I see exactly what's going on,' says God.

'Why don't you take a little road trip to the place in Shiloh, where I first met my people way back in the day? Go look at the ruins. See what I did to it because of how messed up my own people, Israel, were acting.

'So now, because of how you've been living and how you've ignored me, even though I've pulled you aside and talked to you seriously over and over, and because you wouldn't change when I called you to, I'm about to do the same thing to this Temple. This place you think is your safety net, this place I gave to you and your ancestors—I'm going to wreck it, just like I did to Shiloh. And as for you, I'm kicking you out, just like I kicked out your relatives, the people from the northern kingdom of Israel.'

'And Jeremiah, don't even waste your breath praying for these people. Don't bother asking me for favors or trying to step in for them. Don't even bring it up. I'm not listening. Can't you see what they're doing in all the towns of Judah and on the streets of Jerusalem? The kids are out collecting firewood, the dads are building the fires, and the moms are baking bread to offer to the 'Queen of Heaven'! And if that wasn't bad enough, they're pouring out drinks to any other god they can find, just to tick me off.
'But are they really hurting me?' God asks. 'Or are they just hurting themselves? Making themselves look like total fools?

'So here's the deal from the Master God: My super-hot anger is about to get dropped on this whole country—people, animals, trees, crops, everything. It's going to be like a wildfire that no one can put out.'

'Here's a message from the God-of-the-Angel-Armies, Israel's God: Go for it! Add your burnt offerings to all your other sacrifices and have a feast. I definitely don't want them! When I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, I never once told them I wanted burnt offerings and sacrifices. But I did give them this one command: "Obey me. Do what I say, and I'll be your God, and you'll be my people. Live the way I tell you to, so that things will go well for you."

'But did they listen? Not a single word. They just did whatever they wanted, chasing every messed-up idea they had, and they got worse every single day. From the day your ancestors left Egypt until right now, I've sent a non-stop stream of my servants, the prophets, to you. But did the people listen? Nope. Not once. They were stubborn as mules, even worse than their own ancestors!'

'So, tell them all this, but don't be surprised when they don't listen. Yell at them, but don't expect them to answer. Just tell them, "You're the nation that wouldn't listen to God, the one that refused to be disciplined. The truth is gone. You can't even find a trace of it in what you say."
'So go ahead, shave your head. Go up to the hills and cry your eyes out, because God has rejected and abandoned this generation that made him so furious.'

'The people of Judah have been living evil lives right in front of me,' God says. 'As a direct insult, they've put up their disgusting idols in the very Temple that was built to honor me. They've even built altars called Topheth in the Ben-hinnom valley, where they burn their own sons and daughters alive in the fire. That is a twisted perversion of everything I am and everything I command.

'But a time is coming—God's decree!—when no one will call it Topheth or Ben-hinnom anymore. They'll call it Murder Meadow. Dead bodies will be piled up in Topheth because there won't be any other place to bury them! The corpses will be left out in the open for the crows and coyotes to eat. And I'm going to silence all the joy and laughter in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem. No more wedding songs, no more party music. Just dead silence.'

title: God's People Get Cancelled
paragraphs: “Alright, listen up. God’s laying it all out. He says, ‘When the time comes, I’m going to have them dig up the bones of everyone—the kings of Judah, the officials, the priests, the prophets, and yeah, even the regular folks. They’ll spread them all out like they’re worshipping the sun, moon, and stars—all those sky gods they’ve been obsessed with, following their ‘lucky stars’ like lost puppies. The bones will just be left out in the open, turning back into fertilizer. Like straight-up manure.

“And anyone who’s left from this messed-up generation, unlucky enough to still be alive in whatever random place I’ve scattered them to, will wish they were dead.’ That’s the official word from the God of Angel Armies.
“So, tell them this is God’s message:

“‘Yo, do people fall down and just stay there? Or take a wrong turn and keep going? So why are my people going backward and just… staying backward? They’re stubbornly clinging to their own fantasies and refuse to turn around. I listened super carefully, but I didn’t hear a single peep of regret. Not one person said, “My bad.” They just kept on doing their thing, blindly running headfirst into a brick wall. Even cranes know when to fly south for the winter, and all the other birds know when to come back. But my own people? They know nothing. Not the first thing about God and how He runs things.

“‘How can you even say, “We got this. We have God’s playbook”? Look where that’s gotten you—you’re living a lie. Your religious gurus have totally played you! All your ‘smart’ people are about to get exposed, caught, and shown for the frauds they are. I mean, look at them! They know everything *except* God’s Word. You call that being smart?

“‘So here’s what’s gonna happen to your know-it-alls: I’ll give their wives and homes to other people. Everyone, from the bottom to the top, is just chasing money dishonestly. Prophets and priests are all twisting the truth and selling lies. My own people are broken and shattered, and all they do is put on a Band-Aid, saying, “It’s cool, you’ll be fine.” But things are NOT fine! You think they’re embarrassed by this whole disaster? Not at all. They have zero shame. They don’t even know how to blush. It’s hopeless. They’ve hit rock bottom and there’s no getting back up. As far as I’m concerned, they’re done.’ God has spoken.
“‘I went looking to see if I could save anything,’ God says, ‘but there was nothing. Not one grape, not a single fig, just a bunch of dead leaves. I’m taking back everything I ever gave them.’

So why are we just sitting here? Let’s get our act together. Let’s head to the big city and at least go down fighting. God gave us the final word: we’re doomed either way—doomed because we sinned against him. We were hoping for the best, but that’s not what happened. We were waiting for things to get better, and instead, terror showed up. From way up north in Dan, we can hear the sound of horses galloping and neighing. The ground is literally shaking. They’re coming to swallow the whole country, towns and people and all—just fuel for the war.
“‘And on top of that, I’m sending poisonous snakes your way,’ God says. ‘Snakes you can’t charm, snakes that will bite you and you’ll die.’ That’s God’s decree.

I’m drowning in sadness. My heart is sick. Oh, just listen! Can you hear it? It’s the sound of my people crying all over the country. Is God not in Zion anymore? Did the King just leave? Can someone tell me why they’re showing off their toy gods, their worthless, imported fake gods right in front of me? The harvest is over, summer has ended, but for us, nothing has changed. We’re still waiting to be saved. My poor, broken people have left me heartbroken. I’m just weeping, totally overcome with grief. Isn’t there any healing balm in Gilead? Isn’t there a doctor in the house? So why can’t anything be done to heal and save my precious people?”

title: The Ultimate Betrayal & God's Hot Take
paragraphs: Man, I wish my head was a fire hydrant and my eyes were just faucets so I could cry 24/7 for my people. Seriously. Sometimes I just want to run off to a cabin in the middle of nowhere and cut everyone off. They're all so fake, just a bunch of backstabbers.

They shoot lies like they're firing arrows—a whole squad of liars, lowkey allergic to the truth. They go from one bad move to the next and have zero clue who I am, says God. 'Watch your back, even with your day-ones. Don't even trust your own family. Brothers are out here scamming brothers, and friends are spreading fake news about each other. They're always ripping each other off, never being real. They've practiced lying so much, they don't even know what's true anymore. They just keep piling on the bad vibes, lie after lie, and refuse to even get to know me.' That's a direct quote from God.
So, the God of Heaven's Armies says:

'Alright, watch this. I'm about to put them through the fire and see what they're really made of. What else am I supposed to do with people this messed up? Their words are like poison darts. All these fake compliments, like, 'Hey, what's up, hope you're good!' while they're secretly plotting to take you down. You think I'm just gonna sit back and watch this happen?' God's asking. 'You better believe I'm gonna do something major about a nation like this.'

I'm just mourning for the hills and the fields where the animals used to hang out. It's all a wasteland now, too sketchy for anyone to walk through. You can't hear any sheep or cows. Even the birds and wild animals bounced. It's dead silent. God says, 'I'm gonna turn Jerusalem into a pile of rocks, a hangout for stray cats. I'm gonna wreck all the towns in Judah until nobody's left.'
So I asked, 'Yo, is there anyone smart enough to explain what's going on? Anyone who got the inside scoop from God and can fill us in?
Why is the whole country wrecked?
Why is it a ghost town?'

And here's God's answer: 'It's because they ignored my teaching. They wouldn't listen to me or live by my rules. Instead, they just did whatever they felt like and started worshipping these fake Baal gods they thought would give them everything, just like their parents taught them to.' And here's the consequence. The God of Heaven's Armies says:
'I'm gonna make them eat garbage.
'I'm gonna make them drink poison.
'Then I'm gonna scatter them all over the world, to places they've never even heard of, and I'll send Death to chase them until there's no one left.'
A message from the God of Heaven's Armies:

'Take a hard look at the mess we're in and call for backup. Get some singers who can help us mourn what we've lost. Tell them to hurry up—we need to let it all out, get the tears flowing, and make some sad music. Just listen! Listen to the crying coming from Zion: 'We're ruined, we're so ashamed! We've been kicked out of our homes and have to leave our country!''

Hey, all you mourning women! Listen to God's message! Pay attention. Teach your daughters sad songs and your friends songs about heartbreak. Death snuck in through the window and broke into our rooms. Kids are dropping dead on the playground, and young people are collapsing in the middle of their games.
Say it loud! 'God's message:
'Dead bodies will be everywhere, scattered around like manure in a field, like wheat that gets cut and just left to rot.'
God's message:

'Don't let smart people brag about how smart they are. Don't let strong people brag about how strong they are. Don't let rich people brag about how rich they are. If you're gonna brag, brag about this and only this: that you actually get me and know me. I'm God, and I'm all about loyal love. I do what's right and fair, and I love people who do the same. That's my brand.' That's God's decree.

'Heads up! The time is coming,' says God, 'when I'm gonna deal with everyone who's just putting on a show but is empty inside: Egypt, Judah, Edom, Ammon, Moab. All these countries are obsessed with religious rituals—and Israel is no better.'

title: God vs. Stick Gods: The Ultimate Showdown
paragraphs: Yo, Israel, listen up! God's got a message for you, so pay attention.

He's like, 'Don't copy the other nations. Don't get hyped up by all their flashy stuff, even if they think it's cool. Their whole religion is a joke. An idol? It's just a piece of wood someone chopped down and carved. They deck it out with shiny things and nail it down so it doesn't fall over. It's basically a scarecrow that can't even talk. It's dead wood you have to carry around 'cause it can't walk. Seriously, don't be impressed. That stuff is useless—it can't do anything good or bad.'

But man, God, you're on a whole other level. You're seriously great, like, legendary. Who wouldn't be in awe of you, the King of everyone? You're meant to be worshiped! Look at all the so-called 'great' people out there. Their best stuff is nothing compared to you. They're so clueless, lining up these wooden sticks that are good for nothing. They cover them in silver from Tarshish and gold from Uphaz, and dress them up in purple fabrics, but no matter how fancy they look, they're still just sticks.
But God is the real deal—the living God, the forever King. When he gets angry, the whole Earth shakes. And yeah, all those other nations? They're terrified.

So tell them this: 'The fake gods who didn't make the sky or the earth? They're gonna be totally wiped out from the earth and from under the sky.' But it was God who made the earth with his power, who designed the world with his wisdom, and who created the whole universe. When he speaks, it's like thunder, and the rain pours down. He makes the clouds rise up, throws lightning into the storm, and unleashes wind from his storage rooms. The people who worship these stick-gods look so foolish, and the guys who make them are embarrassed by their own creations! Their gods are fakes—just dead sticks, a total joke. When judgment day comes, they'll all turn to ash.
But the God of Jacob is the real thing. He created the entire universe and gives special attention to Israel. His name? The LORD of the Angel Armies!

Grab your stuff, everyone who's being attacked. God's given a warning: 'Attention! I'm kicking out everyone who lives here, right now! I'm about to put the squeeze on them until there's nothing left.'

This is a dark day for me! I'm hopelessly hurt. I was like, 'Man, I really thought I could handle this.' My home is destroyed—the roof is caved in. My kids are gone—I'll never see them again. There's no one left to help me rebuild, no one to help me start over.
It's all because our leaders are so foolish. They never bothered to ask God for advice, so everything went wrong. Now the people are scattered everywhere.
But listen! Something's coming! A huge noise from the north! The towns of Judah are about to get wrecked, left for the wild animals!

I know, God, that we humans can't control our own lives. We don't have what it takes to be in charge. So, God, correct us, but do it gently. Don't lose your temper with us, or we'll be toast. Unleash your anger on the nations that don't know you, on the people who don't even pray to you—the same ones who have totally devoured your people, Jacob, and destroyed everything they have.

title: Plot Twist: They Tried to Cancel Jeremiah
paragraphs: This is a message that came to Jeremiah from God:

"Yo, preach to the people of Judah and everyone in Jerusalem. Tell them this: 'This is God's message, the message from the God of Israel, to you all. Anyone who doesn't stick to the terms of this deal is cursed. The terms are super clear. I laid them out for your ancestors when I rescued them from Egypt, which was basically a furnace of suffering.

'Obey what I tell you. Do exactly what I command. Your obedience will seal the deal. You'll be my people, and I'll be your God. This will make it possible for me to do what I promised your ancestors: to give them a super fertile and awesome land. And, as you know, that's exactly what I did.'"
"For real, God," I replied. "That's true."

God went on: "Preach all this in the towns of Judah and on the streets of Jerusalem. Say, 'Listen to the terms of this deal and actually do them! I warned your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt, and I've been warning you guys ever since. I haven't stopped for a second. I warned them from morning to night: "Obey me or else!" But they didn't. They totally ignored me. They did whatever they wanted, whenever they wanted, until I finally had to step in and bring the punishments I mentioned in the deal, which they had completely ignored despite all my warnings.'"

Then God said, "There's a whole conspiracy going down with the people of Judah and Jerusalem. They've decided to copy the sins of their ancestors—the ones who disobeyed me and started chasing after other gods and worshipping them. Israel and Judah are both in on it, just mindlessly breaking the deal I made with their ancestors.

"Well, your God has something to say about this: Watch out! I'm about to bring some serious doom on you, and nobody's getting out of it. You're all gonna be crying for help, but I won't be listening. Then all the people in Judah and Jerusalem will start praying to the gods you've been sacrificing to for all these years, but it won't help at all. You have as many gods as you have towns, Judah! And you have enough altars for sacrifices to that useless sex god Baal to put one on every street corner in Jerusalem!
"And as for you, Jeremiah, don't even think about praying for these people. Not a word. I'm not going to listen to a single syllable of their crisis prayers."

"What are the people I love even doing trying to get out of trouble? And in my house of worship, no less! Do you really think making promises and coming up with religious programs will save you from doom? Do you think you can get out of this by just being more religious? I once called you a lush, beautiful olive tree, full of good fruit. But it's only going to take one clap of thunder and a bolt of lightning to leave you a total wreck.

"I, the God-of-the-Angel-Armies, who planted you—yep, I'm the one who has declared doom on you. Why? Because of the disastrous life you've lived, both Israel and Judah, making me angry with your constant worship and offerings to that pathetic god Baal."

God told me what was up. That's how I knew. You, God, opened my eyes to their evil plans. I had no clue what was going on—I was like a lamb being led to be slaughtered! I didn't know they were out to get me, didn't know about their secret plots: "Let's get rid of the preacher. That'll stop the sermons! Let's get rid of him for good. No one will even remember him."

Then I said, "God-of-the-Angel-Armies, you're a fair judge. You see and analyze everything people do and think. I want to see these people exposed and taken down! I'm an open book to you. Clear my name."

That got God's attention, and he said: "Here's what I'll do to the men of Anathoth who are trying to kill you, the ones who say, 'Don't preach to us in God's name or we'll kill you.' Yep, it's the God-of-the-Angel-Armies speaking. For real! I'll hold them accountable: Their young men will die in battle, their kids will starve to death, and there will be no one left. I'm bringing doom on the men of Anathoth. It's doomsday!"

title: God, Are You Seeing This?!
paragraphs: God, you're always right, I get it. I can’t even argue. But for real, I have some questions. Why do shady people get to live their best life? Why do scammers get so successful? You set them up, and they're thriving, making bank. They talk about you like you're their bestie, but they honestly couldn't care less. But me? You see right through me. You're always on my case! Make them face the music for how they live, like, for real. End their game. How long do we have to deal with this? The whole country is a mess, farms are failing, and it's all because of these toxic people. Even the animals and birds are dying off because these people have abandoned you and think you've abandoned them.

“So, Jeremiah, if you're already tired from this little race against people, what makes you think you can take on something way bigger? And if you're losing your cool when things are chill, what's gonna happen when real trouble hits, like a massive flood? The people closest to you, your own family, are plotting against you. They're trying to take you down and will do whatever it takes. Don’t trust them, especially when they're acting all nice and friendly.

“I'm gonna have to leave my people, the House of Israel. I'm walking away from them. I'm handing over the ones I love most to their enemies. The one I cared about so much has turned on me, like a lion in the jungle, growling and showing its teeth. I just can't deal with it anymore. Has this person I loved become some kind of flashy, arrogant peacock? But isn't she getting attacked by vultures? Fine, let's invite all the hungry animals to come and get a free meal! Foreign shepherds who just take and take will destroy my fields, turning my beautiful gardens into empty lots full of trash. They'll leave it a total wreck, a sad, ruined land. The whole country is a wasteland, and nobody seems to care.

“Invaders will come from everywhere, swarming over everything. God's sword of judgment will sweep across the land, from one end to the other. Nothing living will be safe. They'll plant wheat but only get weeds. Nothing they do will work out. They'll look at their tiny harvest and just be devastated. This is all because of God's intense anger!”

God’s message was this: “About all the bad neighbors who messed with the land I gave my people Israel: I'm about to kick them out of their own lands, and then I'll get Judah out from the middle of them. Once I've kicked out the bad neighbors, I'll change my mind and be kind to them again, and I'll put them all back where they belong, in their own country, on their own farms. Then, if they get serious about living my way and pray to me, just like they taught my people to pray to that god Baal, then everything will be cool for them. But if they don't listen, I'll rip them out of their land by the roots and throw them in the trash. Total destruction!” That's what God said.

title: Your Pride Is as Rotten as Old Underwear
paragraphs: God hit me up and was like, “Go buy yourself some linen shorts. Put them on and don’t take them off for anything. Seriously, don’t even wash them.” So, I did what God said and bought the shorts and put them on.
Then God told me, “Take those shorts you bought, go straight to the Perath river, and stash them in a crack in a rock.” So I did exactly what God told me and hid them at Perath.

A while later, God said, “Go back to Perath and get the shorts I told you to hide.” So I went back to Perath and dug them out of the spot where I’d hidden them. By then, the shorts were totally rotted and basically worthless.

God broke it down for me: “This is how I’m going to wreck the pride of Judah and the massive ego of Jerusalem. They’re a messed-up crew who won’t listen to me, who just do whatever they feel like, and who chase after a bunch of fake gods and worship them. They’re going to end up as nasty and useless as these old shorts. Just like shorts are supposed to be close to you, I kept the whole family of Israel close to me,”—that’s God’s official word—“so everyone could see they were my people, a crew I could flex on and be proud of. But they straight up refused to do a single thing I said.
“Then you gotta tell them this: ‘This is a message from God, the God of Israel: Every single wine jug should be full of wine.’
“And they’ll be like, ‘Duh. We already know that. Every wine jug should be full of wine!’

“Then you hit them with this: ‘This is what God says: Pay attention. I’m about to get every single person in this country—the kings on David’s throne, the priests, the prophets, all the people of Jerusalem—so drunk they can’t stand up. And then I’m going to smash them, just like smashing those wine-filled jugs—old and young, doesn’t matter. Nothing will stop me. Not one bit of pity or mercy or compassion will make me hesitate. Every last one of you drunken jugs will be shattered!’”

Then I was like, Yo, listen up! Pay attention! Don’t be so stubborn! This is a message from God we’re talking about. Let your lives shine for God before he flips the switch and everything goes dark, before you trip and fall on some dark mountain trail. The light you always just assumed would be there will go out, and the world will turn pitch black. If you guys won’t listen, I’m just gonna go find a corner and cry my eyes out for you. I’ll be crying because you’re so dang arrogant, just bitter, ugly tears. My eyes will be like rivers of tears because God’s own people are going to get dragged off into exile.

Tell the king and the queen mother, “Get off your high horses. Your fancy crowns are about to fall right off your heads.” The towns in the south will be locked down, everyone trapped inside, and all of Judah will be dragged off into exile. The whole country, gone.

Look, Jerusalem! Look at the enemies rolling in from the north! What’s gonna happen to your people, the beautiful flock you were supposed to be taking care of? How are you gonna feel when the very people you were trying to impress, the ones you looked up to for all these years, are now looking down on you? Didn’t see that coming, did you? Surprise! It’s gonna hurt like childbirth. And if I hear you asking, “What’s happening? Why is this happening to me?” The answer is easy: You’re guilty. Super guilty. Your guilt is what put your life on the line, your guilt is why you’re writhing in pain.

Can an African change their skin? Can a leopard just decide to get rid of its spots? So what do you think the chances are of you doing anything good, you who have been practicing how to be evil for so long?

“I’m gonna scatter these people like leaves in the wind. You totally have this coming. I’ve measured out your punishment perfectly.” That’s God’s decree. “It’s all because you forgot me and believed in the Big Lie, that fake god Baal. I’m the one who’s gonna rip your clothes off and expose you in front of the whole world. Your obsessions with all these gods, your affairs with goddesses, your spiritual cheating. Gods on the hills, gods in the fields—every time I turn around, you’re with another one. Oh, Jerusalem, your life is a mess! Is there any hope for you at all?”
