title: God's Ghosting Us & It's Our Fault
paragraphs: God's message about the drought that came to Jeremiah:

"Judah is literally weeping, and its towns are in mourning. The people are just collapsing on the ground, totally miserable, and you can hear Jerusalem's sobbing from miles away. The wealthy sent their servants to get water, but the cisterns were bone dry. They came back with empty buckets, completely panicking and shaking their heads. All the farm work has ground to a halt. Not a single drop of rain. The farmers are at a loss, just wringing their hands and shaking their heads. Even a mother deer ditches her own baby in the field because there's no grass—the fawn's eyes are glazed over, it's on its last legs, basically a skeleton. Wild donkeys are standing on the bare hills, panting like overheated dogs, staring into the distance, waiting for food that's never gonna come."

We know we're the bad guys here. We've lived some seriously bad lives—but please, God, do something. Do it for your own reputation! We've betrayed you over and over. No doubt about it—we've sinned against you. You're the only hope for Israel! Our last chance in all this mess! So why are you acting like a tourist, just checking out the sights, here today and gone tomorrow? Why are you just standing there staring, like someone who has no idea what to do in a crisis? But God, you ARE here, you're with us! You know who we are—you gave us our name! Don't leave us with nothing to stand on.
Then God said this about these people:
"Since they loved to wander off, never thinking about where they were going, I'm done with them—except to call out their guilt and punish their sins."

God told me, "Don't even pray for things to get better for these people. When they fast and pray, I'm not going to listen. When they go overboard with their prayers and bring all sorts of sacrifices, I'm not accepting them. I'm finishing them off with war, famine, and disease."
I said, "But Master, God! Their preachers have been telling them everything's fine—no war, no famine—that it's all good."

Then God said, "Those preachers are liars, and they're using my name to cover up their lies. I never sent them, I never commanded them, and I don't talk to them. The sermons they're passing around are pure fantasy, a web of lies, just whistling in the dark.

"So here's my judgment on them: All the preachers who use my name, who I never sent, who say, 'War and famine will never happen here'—those same preachers will die from war and starvation. And the people they preached to will end up as unburied corpses in the streets of Jerusalem, victims of war and starvation. No funerals for them, their wives, or their kids! I'll make sure they get the full force of their own evil.
"And you, Jeremiah, you'll tell them this:

"'My eyes are pouring out tears. Day and night, they just don't stop. My dear people are battered and bruised, wounded so badly and cruelly it's hopeless. I go out to the fields and I'm shocked by all the dead bodies. I walk into the city and I'm shocked by the sight of starving people. And I see the preachers and priests just going about their business like nothing is wrong!'"

God, have you really given up on Judah for good? Do you just hate Zion now? If not, why have you wrecked us like this, beaten us almost to death? We hoped for peace—and nothing good happened. We looked for healing—and got punched in the gut. We admit it, God, we've lived terribly, and our ancestors were terrible too. We've all sinned against you! Your reputation is on the line! Don't give up on us! Don't abandon your glorious Temple! Remember your promise to us. Don't break your covenant! Can the fake gods of other nations make it rain? Can the sky just water the earth by itself? You're the one, O God, who does this. So you're the one we're waiting for. You made it all, you do it all.

title: God's Done Playing Games
paragraphs: Then God hit me with this: "Jeremiah, for real, even if legends like Moses and Samuel stood right here and tried to argue for them, I wouldn't feel a single thing for these people. Get them out of my sight. Tell them to get lost! And if they have the nerve to ask, 'So, where are we supposed to go?' tell them God's dropping the facts:
'If you're slated to die, go die. If you're assigned to the battlefield, go get taken out. If you're meant to starve, go starve. If you're getting exiled, then get to stepping!'

"I've got four kinds of punishment all set up: death in battle, corpses getting dragged off by killer dogs, the rest picked clean by vultures, and the bones gnawed on by hyenas. They're gonna be a horror show, a sight that will shock the whole world—and it's all because of Manasseh, son of Hezekiah, and all the messed-up stuff he did in Jerusalem.
"Who do you think is gonna feel sorry for you, Jerusalem? Who's gonna waste tears on you? Who's even gonna bother to hit you up and ask, 'Yo, you good?'

"You left me, remember?" This is God's official decree. "You turned your back and just walked out. So now I'm gonna grab you and hit you hard. I'm so tired of letting you off the hook. I tossed you to the four winds and let you get scattered like leaves. I'm making sure you lose everything, since nothing ever makes you change. I've made more widows among you than there are grains of sand on all the beaches. At noon, moms are gonna get the news that their sons were killed in action. Just sudden pain for the mothers—all those awful deaths. A mom with seven kids just collapses, gasping for air, robbed of her children in their prime. Her sun sets in the middle of the day! Then I'll round up whoever is left and make sure your enemies finish you off." God's decree.

I was like, unlucky me that my mom had me as a son, stuck with the miserable job of calling out the whole country! I've never hurt or scammed a single person, and yet everyone is out to get me. But God, you know I've done everything I could to help them, prayed for them and against their enemies. I've always been on their team, trying to stop the disaster. God, you know how hard I've tried!

"Oh Israel, oh Judah, what are your chances against the iron giant from the north? As punishment for your sins, I'm giving away all your stuff, giving it away for free. I'm gonna make you slaves to your enemies in some weird, far-off country. My anger is blazing hot, burning in judgment against you."

God, you know what's up! Remember what I'm doing out here! Take my side against all these haters. Don't just stand there while they wreck me. Just look at all this suffering I'm going through for you! When your words showed up, I ate them—I literally swallowed them whole. And it was a feast! I was so stoked to be yours, O God, God-of-the-Angel-Armies! I never hung out with the party crowd, laughing and having fun. You led me, so I went off by myself. You had filled me with so much anger. Their sin had me absolutely seething. But why, God, why this constant pain, this wound that just gets worse with no healing in sight? You're like a mirage, a beautiful oasis that looks real from a distance—and then it's just nothing!
This is how God answered me:

"Take back those words, and I'll take you back. Then you'll stand tall in my presence. Use real, meaningful words. Don't stoop to cheap whining. Then, and only then, you'll be my spokesperson. Let your words change them. Don't you dare change your words to fit in with them. I'll make you a steel wall, a thick, unbreakable steel wall. They'll come at you but won't even put a dent in you, because I'm right by your side, defending and delivering you." God's decree. "I'll deliver you from the grip of the wicked. I'll get you out of the clutch of the ruthless."

title: God's Done with Fake People
paragraphs: So God hit me up with this message:

He was like, 'Jeremiah, don't even think about getting married or having kids around here. I've basically signed off on a death sentence for every kid born in this place, their moms, and their dads. It's gonna be a total plague of death. No one's gonna cry, no one's gonna get a burial. Their bodies will just be left out to rot and stink, like actual trash. And all the people killed or starved? They're just gonna be food for crows and stray dogs.'

God kept going: 'Don't go into a house where people are mourning. Don't go to any funerals. Don't even act sympathetic. I'm so over caring about these people.' That was God's official word. 'No more loyal love from me, no more feeling sorry for them. Famous people, regular people, they're all gonna die the same, with no one to mourn them or bury them. No funerals, no one will even care enough to say 'that's tough,' or bring a cup of tea to a grieving parent.'
'And if there's a party going on, don't you dare go and have a good time.'

The God-of-the-Angel-Armies, the God of Israel, says, 'Yo, watch this. I'm about to make this place a total fun-free zone. No more smiles, no more laughter. No more weddings. And it's happening in your lifetime, right before your eyes.'

'When you tell everyone this, they're gonna be like, 'Why is God being so harsh, threatening us with all this crazy stuff? We're not bad people. What did we do to our God to get treated like this?' You tell them this: 'It's because your ancestors totally abandoned me. They just walked away and started worshipping fake gods, doing whatever they wanted, and completely ignored me and my rules. And you guys are even worse! Seriously, take a look at yourselves—you're all just doing whatever you want, whenever you want, and not paying any attention to me. So because of that, I'm kicking you out, shipping you off to some weird, foreign country. You can worship your precious fake gods there all you want. Trust me, I won't bother you again.'

'But also, don't sleep on this: The time is coming when people won't say, 'As sure as God lives, the God who saved Israel from Egypt.' Instead, they'll say, 'As sure as God lives, the God who brought Israel back from the land up north, and from all the other places he scattered them.' That's right, I'm gonna bring them back to the land I originally gave their ancestors.'

'Now, get ready for what's next: I'm about to gather a bunch of fishermen.' This is God's decree. 'They're gonna go fishing for my people and reel them in for judgment. Then, I'll send out a crew of hunters, and they'll track them down in all the mountains, hills, and caves. I'm watching every single move they make. I haven't lost sight of a single one of them, or their sins.'

'They're not getting away with anything. They'll pay back double for all the wrong they did. They've made a complete disaster of everything, cluttering up their lives with their gross fake gods, leaving piles of stinking god-junk all over my land.'

God, you're my strength, my fortress, my safe place when things get crazy. The nations who don't know you will come from all over the world, saying, 'Our ancestors believed in straight-up lies, useless things that were all smoke and mirrors.' Can people actually make their own gods? Nah, the stuff they make are just no-gods!
'So watch closely now. I'm gonna teach these clueless people a lesson. Starting right now, I'm gonna show them who I am and what I can do. I'll teach them the meaning of my name, God—'I Am.''
changes: 슬랭 수정 (Rule 3): 'totally ghosted me' → 'totally abandoned me'

title: Who Do You REALLY Trust?
paragraphs: Judah's sin is basically etched in stone, carved with a steel pen with a diamond tip right onto their hearts and the corners of their altars. The proof is everywhere: those sketchy altars and shrines for sex and religion are all over the place, under every green tree and on every high hill.

God says, "I'm gonna let people just take all your stuff from your mountain hideouts. All your possessions will be the price for your sins throughout the country. You're gonna lose the land I gave you, your inheritance. I'll make you slaves to your enemies in a country you've never even seen. My anger is blazing hot, and it's not going out."
This is what God's saying:

"You're cursed if you're one of those people who relies on other humans, who thinks you can get by on your own strength and just pushes God to the side. You'll be like a dried-up bush in the desert, totally disconnected from anything good. You'll live a pointless life in a barren land where nothing grows.

"But you're blessed if you trust in me, God. You're like a tree planted by a river, with roots that reach deep into the water. You won't be stressed during hot summers or worry when there's a drought. You'll stay green and keep producing fruit no matter what.

"The human heart is the most deceitful thing ever, it's a total mystery that no one can figure out. But I, God, can see right through it. I check out the heart and the mind to get to the real you. I see what's really going on and treat you accordingly, not based on how you act on the outside."
"A person who gets rich by cheating is like a bird that lays its eggs in another bird's nest. When the truth comes out, they'll look like a total fool."

"Your Temple has always been a glorious and honored throne from the very beginning! God, you are the hope of Israel. Anyone who leaves you will end up looking like a fool. They're deserters who walk away from you, the source of living water, and they'll end up with nothing.

"God, please fix me and make me whole again. You're the one I praise! But listen to what they're saying about me: 'Where is this so-called Word of God? We want to see some action!' But I never asked for all this drama and destruction. You know everything I've said; it's all out in the open. Don't make things harder for me. Give me a break! Let the people who are giving me a hard time be the ones who get embarrassed, not me. Let them be the ones who face your judgment. Bring on the day of doom for them. Drop the hammer!"

God's message to me was: "Go stand at the People's Gate, where the kings of Judah come and go, and then go to all the other gates of Jerusalem. Tell them, 'Listen up, kings of Judah, and all you people of Jerusalem who use these gates! This is God's message!'

"'God says, if you value your life, you better not treat the Sabbath like any other day. Don't be carrying your stuff around and doing business. Keep the Sabbath day holy, just like I told your ancestors. But they didn't listen, as you know. They ignored me and did their own thing, refusing to be guided by me.'

"'But if you actually listen to me and stop treating the Sabbath as a regular workday, and keep it holy, then kings from David's line will continue to rule. They and their officials will ride through these gates on horses and in chariots. The people of Judah and Jerusalem will keep passing through, and this city will always be full of people. They will come from all over Judah, from the nearby towns, the foothills, the mountains, and the desert. They'll bring all kinds of offerings to worship in my Temple.'

"'But if you don't listen to me and don't keep the Sabbath holy, and you keep doing your own thing on that day, then I will burn down the gates of this city. I'll burn down the whole city, including the palaces, with a fire that no one can put out!'"

title: God, the OG Potter, and Us
paragraphs: God hit up Jeremiah and was like, “Yo, get up and go to the potter’s house. When you get there, I’ll tell you what’s up.”

So I bounced to the potter’s place, and for real, the potter was there, just doing his thing at the wheel. Whenever the pot he was making got messed up, like clay stuff sometimes does, he’d just scrap it and start over with the same clay to make a new one.

Then God’s message dropped: “Yo, people of Israel, can’t I do the same thing this potter is doing?” This is God’s decree. “Watch this potter. Just like he works his clay, I’m working on you, people of Israel. One minute I might be like, ‘I’m about to uproot a whole nation and get rid of them.’ But if they turn away from their messed-up lives, I’ll have a change of heart and start fresh with them. Then another time, I might decide to build up a nation, but if they don’t connect with me and won’t listen, I’ll rethink my plans for them and just dip.”

“So, go tell the people of Judah and Jerusalem my message: ‘Danger! I’m literally shaping disaster for you, making plans against you. You gotta turn back from your self-destructing lifestyle. Get your lives straight, for real.’”
“But they’ll just be like, ‘Nah, why? What’s the point? We’re just gonna keep living how we’ve always lived, disaster or not.’”
God’s message:

“Go ask around. Check with the nations that don’t even believe. Has anyone ever heard of something this wild? Virgin Israel has become a total shameless woman! Does snow just vanish from the mountains in Lebanon? Do mountain streams just dry up? But my people have abandoned me to worship a complete lie. They’ve strayed from the right path, the one everyone knows, and now they’re just stumbling through the weeds and getting tangled up. Their country is gonna end up a total wreck—a joke that everyone spits on. People passing by will just shake their heads, like, ‘Wow.’ I’ll scatter my people in front of their enemies like leaves in a hurricane. On their judgment day, all they’ll see is my back as I walk away, not even a glimpse of my face.”

Some of the people were like, “Come on, let’s scheme against Jeremiah. We still have priests to teach us, smart people to give us advice, and prophets to tell us what God’s saying. Let’s just cancel him so we don’t have to deal with him anymore.”
And I was like, to God:

“God, you hear this? Just listen to what my haters are saying. Should I get shade for doing good? ‘Cause that’s what they’re doing. They’ve literally plotted to kill me! Remember all the times I went to bat for them, speaking up for them, trying to get you to chill out? But I’m done! Let their kids starve! Let them get wrecked in battle! Let their wives lose their kids and their husbands, let their friends die, and let their cocky young men get taken out. Let their homes be filled with screams of panic when you ambush them with surprise attacks! They’re all plotting to kill me! But you know all this, God. You know they’re dead set on killing me. Don’t just ignore their crimes, don’t let a single sin slide! Round them all up in front of you. Strike while your anger is hot!”
changes: 슬랭 수정 (Rule 1): 'don’t vibe with me' → 'don’t connect with me'
슬랭 수정 (Rule 3): 'have ghosted me to worship' → 'have abandoned me to worship'

title: The Smashed Pot Prophecy
paragraphs: God hit me up and said, “Go buy a clay pot. Then grab a few of the city leaders and some head priests and head out to the Valley of Ben-hinnom, right outside the Potsherd Gate. Preach the message I give you there.

“Say, ‘Listen up to God’s Word, you kings of Judah and people of Jerusalem! This is the message from the God-of-the-Angel-Armies, the God of Israel. I’m about to bring a disaster on this place that will make everyone’s ears ring. It’s a disaster because they’ve totally abandoned me and made this place weird by worshiping random gods—gods they, their parents, and the old kings of Judah had never even heard of. It’s a disaster because they’ve murdered innocent people here. It’s a disaster because they’ve built altars to that fake god Baal and burned their own kids alive as offerings to him. That’s a horrific act I never commanded, never even hinted at!

“‘So, payback time is coming,’ God declares. ‘This place won’t be called Topheth or the Valley of Ben-hinnom anymore. It’s gonna be called Massacre Meadows. I’m trashing all of Judah and Jerusalem’s plans for this place, and I’ll have their enemies kill them. I’ll leave their dead bodies for birds and wild animals to eat. I’m going to make this city a showcase of horror. Anyone who passes by will be shocked speechless by the brutality. The people will literally become cannibals. The stress from the enemy siege will be so intense, they’ll eat their own children! Yeah, they’ll start eating each other—family and friends and all.’

“Say all this, and then smash the pot right in front of the men who came with you. Then say, ‘This is what the God-of-the-Angel-Armies says: I’m going to smash this nation and this city just like someone smashes a clay pot so bad it can’t be fixed. They’ll be burying bodies here in Topheth until there’s no space left. And this whole city will become one big Topheth. The city, from the people to the kings, will be turned into a place for worshiping star gods and goddesses, basically becoming a giant open grave, stinking like a sewer, just like Topheth.’”

Then Jeremiah left Topheth, where God had sent him to preach, and stood in the courtyard of God’s Temple. He said to all the people, “This is the message from the God-of-the-Angel-Armies to you: ‘Warning! I’m bringing down on this city and all the nearby towns the disaster I promised. You’re all so stubborn and refuse to listen to a single thing I say.’”
changes: 슬랭 수정 (Rule 3): 'they’ve totally ghosted me' → 'they’ve totally abandoned me'

title: Jeremiah's Public Meltdown & God's Promise
paragraphs: So, there was this head priest, Pashur, the son of Immer, who was basically the top dog at God's Temple. He heard Jeremiah giving this speech and got super mad. He had Jeremiah whipped and then locked him up in the stocks at the Benjamin Gate of the Temple. The next day, Pashur lets him out, and Jeremiah just looks at him and goes, 'God's got a new nickname for you. It's not Pashur anymore; it's 'Mr. Danger-From-Every-Side.' Because God's saying you're a walking disaster, not just for you but for everyone. All your friends are gonna die in battle, and you're just gonna stand there and watch. And get this: God's handing over all of Judah to the king of Babylon. He can do whatever he wants—drag them off to another country, kill them for no reason. Everything valuable in this city, all the property, the fancy stuff, even the king's own treasure—it's all going to the enemy. They're gonna take whatever they want and haul it back to Babylon.

'And as for you, Pashur, you and your whole family are getting shipped off as prisoners to Babylon. You're gonna die there and be buried there, along with all your buddies you told all those lies to.'

God, you totally dragged me into this, and I just went along with it. You were just too strong for me. And now? I'm a total joke. Everyone makes fun of me. Every time I try to say something, I'm just screaming about violence and disaster. And what do I get for sharing your warnings? Just insults and people treating me like trash. But if I try to be like, 'Okay, I'm done. No more messages from God,' the words just burn inside me, like a fire in my bones. I'm exhausted from trying to keep it all in. I can't do it! Then I hear them whispering about me, like, 'There goes old 'Mr. Danger.' Let's shut him up! Let's report him!' Even my old friends are just waiting for me to mess up so they can be like, 'Gotcha! We'll finally be rid of him.'

But God, you're on my side, like a seriously fierce warrior. The people chasing me are going to trip and fall flat on their faces. They'll be a total joke, completely humiliated, and no one will ever forget it.

Oh, God of the Angel Armies, you see everything. No one can fool you. You know what's really going on inside everyone. I really want to see you give them what they deserve. I'm leaving it in your hands.
Sing to God! Give God all the praise! He saves the underdog from the clutches of the wicked.

Man, curse the day I was born! Seriously, the day my mom had me—I wish it was cursed. And curse the guy who ran to my dad all excited, like, 'It's a boy!' and made him so happy. I wish that news had never been delivered, like it was deleted from history. And the guy who brought the news? I hope his life is just full of bad news. He should've just killed me in the womb. My mom's womb should've been my grave, and she should've just been pregnant forever with a dead baby. Why did I ever have to be born? My life has been nothing but stress and sadness, and it feels like it's just going to be more of the same.

title: God's Ultimate Warning: Surrender or Get Wrecked
paragraphs: So, King Zedekiah sent two guys, Pashur son of Malkijah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, to Jeremiah with a message. They were like, "Yo, Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, is about to attack us. Can you please pray to God for us? Maybe God will pull off one of his classic miracles and make him bounce."

But Jeremiah hit them back with this: "Go tell Zedekiah that this is what the God of Israel is saying: Your army is basically toast. All your weapons and morale? Going straight down the drain. I'm personally gonna lead the king of Babylon and his crew, the ones you're trying so hard to fight, right into the middle of your city. Yeah, you heard that right. I'm teaming up with them and fighting against you. I'm going all out, no holding back, and I'm seriously angry. I'm about to wipe out everyone in this city, people and animals, with a crazy plague. Then, I'll personally hand over King Zedekiah, his officials, and anyone who's left alive to King Nebuchadnezzar. He's gonna take them out without any mercy."

"And then, tell everyone else, God's message is this: Listen up. I'm giving you a choice: life or death. Anyone who stays in this city is gonna die—from the fighting, starvation, or sickness. But if you walk out and surrender to the Babylonians surrounding the city, you'll live. You'll lose all your stuff, but you'll save your own skin. I'm dead serious about destroying this city. That's how mad I am at this place, God says. I'm handing it over to the king of Babylon, and he's going to burn it to the ground."

"And to the royal family of Judah, listen to God's message! House of David, for real, listen up: God's telling you to start every day by actually doing what's right. Stand up for people who are getting taken advantage of. You better stop this, or my anger is gonna flare up like a fire that no one can put out. Your whole corrupt system is just fuel for my anger. You seriously don't get that I'm against you, do you? You think you're all safe and sound, saying, 'Who could possibly get to us? Who can crash our party?' Well, guess what? I can, and I will. I'm gonna punish your messed-up government. I'll start a fire that'll burn completely out of control and turn everything you see into ashes."
changes: 복원: son of Malkijah, son of Maaseiah (MSG 기준)

title: God's EPIC Rant at the King's Palace
paragraphs: God's orders: "Yo, head over to the royal palace and drop this message. Tell the king of Judah, who's chilling on David's throne, and his whole crew and all the people coming in and out of the palace gates to listen up. This is God's message: Start actually caring about justice. Make things right between people. Rescue the people who are getting taken advantage of. Don't mess with the homeless, the orphans, or the widows. And for real, stop all the murdering!

"If you guys actually follow these commands, then kings from David's line will keep rolling in and out of these palace gates on horses and in chariots—them, their officials, and all the people of Judah. But if you don't listen to what I'm saying, then I swear on my own name—God's decree!—this whole palace is gonna end up as a pile of rubble."
This is God's final word on Judah's royal palace:

"I literally put you on a pedestal, like you were as awesome as the hills of Gilead or the peaks of Lebanon. But I swear I'm about to turn you into a total wasteland, like a ghost town. I'm gonna hire a demolition crew, and they're coming with sledgehammers and wrecking bars to tear this country down and burn it all up.

"People from all over are gonna come through here and ask each other, 'Yo, why would God do something so wild to this amazing city?' And they'll be told, 'It's because they broke their promise to their God, and started chasing after other gods and worshiping them.'"
Don't cry for King Josiah who died. Don't waste your tears on him. Instead, cry for his son who got exiled. He's gone for good and he's never coming home.

Because this is God's word on Shallum, Josiah's son, who became king of Judah after his dad: "He's gone from here, for good. He's gonna die in the country they took him to. He's never gonna see his home again."

"You're done for. You build these fancy palaces by bullying people, and you make a nice house for yourself by destroying other people's lives. You cheat your workers and don't even pay them for their work. You're all like, 'I'm gonna build myself a huge mansion with big rooms and cool windows. I'll get all this rare, expensive wood and the newest interior design.' So, you think that makes you a king—living in a fancy palace? Your dad did just fine, didn't he? He did what was right and treated people fairly, and things went well for him. He stood up for the poor and the helpless, and things went well for Judah. Isn't that what it really means to know me?" God's decree! "But you're just blind and clueless. All you think about is yourself, taking advantage of the weak, bulldozing your way through life, and hurting people."

This is God's final message for Jehoiakim, son of Josiah, king of Judah: "This guy is doomed. No one's gonna cry for him and say, 'Oh, my poor brother!' No one's gonna cry for him and say, 'Oh, my poor master!' He's gonna get a donkey's funeral—they'll just drag his body out of the city and dump it somewhere.

"People of Jerusalem, go up to a mountain in Lebanon and cry, go up to a mountain in Bashan and wail, go up to the Abarim ridge and just cry your eyes out—you've completely messed up your life. I tried to talk to you when everything was going great for you. But you were like, 'I'm not interested.' You've been like that for as long as I've known you, you've never listened to a single thing I said. All your leaders are gonna be blown away, and all your friends are gonna end up in exile. And then you'll be left in the gutter, totally disgraced because of your evil life. You big-city people thought you were so important, like you were the 'king of the mountain'! But you're about to be doubled over in pain, a pain that's even worse than childbirth.

"As sure as I am the living God"—God's decree—"even if you, Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim king of Judah, were the special ring on my right hand, I'd pull you off and give you to the people who are trying to kill you, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and the Chaldeans. And then I'm gonna throw you and your mom into a foreign country, far away from where you were born. And you'll both die there.
"You'll be so homesick, like desperately homesick, but you'll never get to go home again."

Is Jehoiachin just a leaky bucket, a rusty old pail that's good for nothing? Why else would he and his kids be thrown away, just tossed into a foreign country? Oh land, land, land, listen to God's message! This is God's final decision: "Write this man off as if he never had kids, a man who will never be successful. Nothing will ever come of his life. He's the end of the line, the last of the kings."

title: God vs. the Fake Prophets
paragraphs: “It’s game over for the so-called leaders who are messing up and scattering my people,” God says. “So listen up, this is what I, the God of Israel, have to say to the shepherds who’ve been leading my people astray: ‘You’ve scattered my flock, you’ve driven them off, and you haven’t looked out for them. Well, I’ve been looking at you, and I’ve seen all your messed-up behavior. I’m taking over. I’ll gather what’s left of my sheep from all the places I’ve scattered them. I’ll bring them back to their home, and they’ll start fresh and flourish. I’ll set up new leaders who will actually take care of them. They won’t have to be scared or stressed anymore. All the lost sheep will be found!’ That’s a promise from God.

“The time is coming,” God declares, “when I’ll raise up a righteous King from David’s line, a ruler who actually knows how to rule. He’ll bring justice and unite the people. In his time, Judah will be safe, and Israel will live in peace. And this is the name he’ll be known by: ‘The God Who Makes Everything Right.’

“So watch out for this. A time is coming,” says God, “when people won’t say, ‘As sure as God lives, the one who brought Israel out of Egypt,’ but they’ll say, ‘As sure as God lives, the one who brought the descendants of Israel back from the north and all the other countries where he’d sent them, so they can live in their own land again.’”
My head is spinning, my body feels weak, I’m stumbling around like I’m drunk, and it’s all because of God and his powerful words.
Now, here’s what God has to say about the lying prophets:

“Can you believe this? The whole country is full of people who are unfaithful to God, obsessed with idols. They’re a curse on the land, and it’s turning into a wasteland. Their unfaithfulness is making the country a toxic mess. Prophets and priests are disrespecting me, even in my own Temple. It’s covered in the filth of their crimes,” says God. “But they won’t get away with it. They’re on a slippery slope, heading straight for darkness. I’ll make them pay for their crimes. It’s going to be the Year of Doom,” God declares.

“In Samaria, I saw prophets acting like fools, preaching in the name of the fake god Baal and messing with my people’s minds. But the prophets in Jerusalem are even worse. It’s horrible. They’re driven by their own selfish desires, living a lie, and encouraging a culture of wickedness without a second thought. They’re as bad as the people of Sodom and Gomorrah.”
So here’s the message to the prophets from God-of-the-Angel-Armies:
“I’ll feed them a meal of maggots and a drink of poison. The prophets in Jerusalem are the source of all this godlessness that’s polluting the country.”
A Message from God-of-the-Angel-Armies:

“Don’t listen to the sermons of these prophets. It’s all just hot air and lies. They make it all up; not a single word comes from me. They preach ‘Everything will be fine’ to people who don’t care about God, and ‘Nothing bad will happen to you’ to people who are stuck in their own ways.

“Have any of these prophets actually met with me, the true God? Have they bothered to listen to what I have to say and then live it out? Watch out! God’s hurricane is coming, a whirlwind that will spin the heads of the wicked. God’s anger won’t stop until I’ve finished the job I started. When it’s all over, you’ll see that it was the right thing to do.

“I never sent these prophets, but they ran off to preach anyway. I never spoke to them, but they couldn’t stop talking. If they had actually taken the time to meet with me, they would have preached my message to my people. They would have helped them get back on the right track and out of their evil ways.
“Am I not a God who is near,” says God, “and not a God who is far away? Can anyone hide in a corner where I can’t see them?” God asks. “Am I not everywhere, whether you see me or not?”

“I know what they’re saying, all these prophets who preach lies in my name, saying, ‘I had a dream! I had a dream!’ How long do I have to put up with this? Do these prophets even care about me as they preach their lies and their own delusions? They share their fake dreams with each other, trying to make my people forget about me, just like their ancestors forgot about me for the fake god Baal.

“You prophets who only have dreams, go ahead and tell your silly stories. But you prophets who have a message from me, tell it faithfully. What does straw have in common with wheat? My message is like fire,” says God. “It’s like a sledgehammer that can break a rock.
“I’m done with the ‘prophets’ who just copy each other’s sermons. I’ve had it with them. They make things up and pretend it’s a real message from me.
“Oh yes, I’ve had it with the prophets who preach the lies they dream up, spreading them all over the country and ruining my people’s lives with their cheap and reckless lies.
“I never sent these prophets, and I never authorized a single one of them. They do nothing for this people—nothing!” says God.
“And if anyone, including prophets and priests, asks, ‘What’s God’s message? What’s troubling him?’ you tell them, ‘You’re the trouble, and I’m getting rid of you,’” says God.
“And if anyone, including prophets and priests, goes around casually saying, ‘This is God’s message!’, I’ll punish them and their family.

“Instead of pretending to know what God says, ask each other questions like, ‘How do we understand God in this?’ But don’t go around acting like you know it all, saying, ‘God told me this… God told me that…’ I don’t want to hear it anymore. Only the person I authorize can speak for me. Otherwise, my message gets twisted, the message of the living God-of-the-Angel-Armies.

“You can ask the prophets, ‘How did God answer you? What did he tell you?’ But don’t pretend you know all the answers and talk like you’re experts. I’m telling you, stop with the ‘God told me this… God told me that…’ talk.

“Are you paying attention? You better be, because I’m about to grab you and this whole city that I gave to your ancestors and throw you to the ground. I’ve had enough of all of you. You’re never going to live this down. You’ll go down in history as a total disgrace.”

title: Good Figs vs. Rotten Figs: Who's Who?
paragraphs: So, God showed me this vision: two baskets of figs sitting in front of His Temple. This happened right after King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon had dragged King Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim, the leaders of Judah, and all the skilled workers from Jerusalem into exile in Babylon. One basket was full of amazing, perfectly ripe figs. The other one was full of nasty, rotten figs that were completely inedible.
God asked me, “Jeremiah, what do you see?”
I said, “Figs. Some are super good, the best quality, and the others are totally rotten, so bad you can’t eat them.”

Then God laid it all out for me: “This is the message from the God of Israel: The people I sent to Babylon are like the good figs, and I’m going to treat them well. I’ll watch over them, make sure their lives are good, and bring them back to this land. I’m going to build them up, not tear them down. I’ll plant them, not pull them up.
“I’ll give them a heart that truly knows me as God. They will be my people, and I will be their God, because they will come back to me with everything they’ve got.

“But Zedekiah, the king of Judah, and his officials, and all the people left in Jerusalem or living in Egypt—they’re like those rotten figs. That’s how I’ll treat them. I’ll make them a horror show for the whole world to see. They'll be outcasts, and their names will become a curse everywhere I scatter them. I’ll send war, famine, and plagues after them until they are completely wiped out from the land I gave to their ancestors.”

title: God's Wrath is a Cup and EVERYONE'S Drinking
paragraphs: Alright, so this is the word that came to Jeremiah for everyone in Judah. It all went down in the fourth year that Jehoiakim, Josiah’s son, was king of Judah. This was also the first year Nebuchadnezzar was king of Babylon.
The prophet Jeremiah laid out this message for all the people of Judah and everyone living in Jerusalem:

"Listen up. For the last 23 years, starting from the thirteenth year Josiah son of Amon was king all the way to today, God's Word has been hitting me up, and I've been passing it on to you guys from morning till night. And you haven't listened to a single thing!

"And not only that, but God also sent a whole squad of prophets your way who were just as relentless as me, and you still didn't listen. They were all like, 'Yo, turn back—like, right now!—from your messed-up lifestyle and bad choices, and actually live in the land God gave you and your ancestors, the land he wanted you to have forever. Stop chasing after all these trendy fake gods, bowing down to these no-gods. Don't make me mad with your little god-making side hustles—that's a dangerous game!'
"But you guys just refused to listen, and now I'm seriously ticked off. This whole business of making your own gods? It's gonna be your downfall."

So, here's the verdict from God-of-the-Angel-Armies on all this: "Because you’ve turned away from me and ignored what I said, I'm stepping in. I'm calling up the armies from the north, led by King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon—he's my servant in all this—and I'm unleashing them on this land, its people, and even the countries around you. I'm dedicating this whole place to total destruction. It's gonna be a horror show unlike anything in history. And I’ll get rid of every sound of joy—no more singing, laughing, wedding parties, chill workers, or candlelit dinners. The whole country will be a giant wasteland. These nations will be under the thumb of the king of Babylon for seventy years.

"But once those seventy years are up, I'll punish the king of Babylon and the entire nation of Babylon for their sin. Then they'll become the wasteland. Everything I said I'd do to that country, I'll do—everything written in this book, everything Jeremiah preached against all the godless nations. A bunch of nations and powerful kings will enslave the Babylonians, paying them back for everything they did. They won't get away with a thing." That's God's decree.

This is a message the God of Israel gave me: "Take this cup filled with the wine of my anger that I'm handing you. Make all the nations where I send you drink it. They'll drink it and get wasted, stumbling around in a daze because of the slaughter I'm about to unleash on them."
So I took the cup from God’s hand and made them all drink it, every nation he sent me to:
Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, with their kings and leaders, turning them into a huge wasteland, a horror story, a cussword—which, let's be real, they are now;
Pharaoh king of Egypt with his crew and leaders, plus all his people and the whole mix of foreigners there;
All the kings of Uz;
All the kings of the Philistines from Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and what's left of Ashdod;
Edom, Moab, and the Ammonites;
All the kings of Tyre, Sidon, and the coastlands across the sea;
Dedan, Tema, Buz, and the nomads on the edge of the desert;
All the kings of Arabia and the various Bedouin chiefs wandering in the desert;
All the kings of Zimri, Elam, and the Medes;
All the kings from the north, near and far, one after another;
Basically all the kingdoms on planet Earth...
And the king of Sheshak (aka Babylon) will be the last one to drink.
"Tell them, 'These are orders from God-of-the-Angel-Armies, the God of Israel: Drink, get wasted, and puke. Fall flat on your faces and don't get up. You're all scheduled for a massacre.'
"If any of them refuse to take the cup from you and drink, tell them, 'God-of-the-Angel-Armies has ordered you to drink. So drink up!'

"'Get ready for the worst! I'm starting this disaster in the city that's supposed to be mine, so you really think you're gonna get away with it? Nah, you're not getting out of anything. It's the sword, and only the sword, for everyone, everywhere!'" The decree from God-of-the-Angel-Armies.
"Preach all of it, Jeremiah. Give them the whole message. Say:

"'God roars like a lion from way up high; thunder booms from his holy place—deafening roars against his people, shouting like workers at harvest time. The noise echoes all over the earth; everyone everywhere hears it. God is bringing a case against the godless nations. He's about to put the whole human race on trial. For the wicked, the verdict is simple: death by the sword.'" God's Decree.
A message from God-of-the-Angel-Armies:
"Brace yourselves! It's doomsday! Disaster is spreading from nation to nation. A massive storm is about to hit the entire planet."

Lined up end to end, the people killed by God's judgment that day will stretch from one side of the earth to the other. No one will cry for them or bury them. Their bodies will just be left where they fall, like manure spread over a field.

"Wail, you shepherds! Scream for help! Roll around in the dirt, you leaders of the flock! Your time is up—you're headed for the slaughterhouse, like a prize ram about to get its throat cut. There's no escape for the rulers, no getting away for you shepherds. You hear that? Rulers crying for help, flock leaders wailing! God is about to destroy their nice pastures. The peaceful sheepfolds will go silent with death, silenced by God's killer anger. God will come out like a lion from its den, and the country will be torn apart, ripped up and destroyed by his rage."

title: Prophesy in God's Name & Get Canceled?
paragraphs: Right at the start of King Jehoiakim's rule (he was Josiah's son), God hit up Jeremiah with this message.

God said, "Yo, stand in the courtyard of my Temple. Preach to all the people coming from all over Judah to worship. Say every single thing I tell you. Don't sugarcoat it. Maybe, just maybe, they'll actually listen and turn back from their messed-up lives. If they do, I'll rethink the disaster I'm planning to drop on them for all their evil actions.

"Tell them, 'This is what God's saying: If you refuse to listen to me and live by the rules I've laid out so clearly for you, and if you keep ignoring my servants the prophets that I keep sending your way—not that you've ever listened before, so why start now?—then I'm gonna make this Temple a total wreck like Shiloh, and I'll make this city a global laughingstock.'"

Everyone there—the priests, the prophets, and all the people—heard Jeremiah saying all this in God's Temple. The second Jeremiah finished his sermon, saying everything God told him to, the priests, prophets, and the crowd all grabbed him, yelling, "You're dead! You're gonna die for this! How dare you use God's name to say this Temple will become a pile of rubble like Shiloh and this city will be wiped out with no one left?!"
And just like that, the whole crowd mobbed Jeremiah right there in the Temple.

The officials at the king's palace got word of what was happening. They bounced from the palace and rushed over to God's Temple to see what was up. They set up a court right on the spot, at the New Gate entrance.

The priests and prophets went first, talking to the officials but making sure the crowd heard too: "This guy deserves to die! He's been preaching against our city—you all heard him with your own ears."

Then it was Jeremiah's turn. He spoke to the officials and the whole crowd: "God sent me to say all this stuff against the Temple and the city. So, like, do something about it! Change how you're living, fix your behavior. Actually listen to what your God is telling you. Maybe God will call off the disaster he threatened.

"As for me, I'm in your hands. Do whatever you think is right. But let me give you a heads-up: if you kill me, you're killing an innocent man. And you, this city, and everyone in it will be responsible. I didn't just make this up. God sent me and told me exactly what to say. You've been listening to God, not me."
Then the officials, with the people backing them up, gave their verdict to the priests and prophets: "Not guilty. No death sentence for this man. He was speaking to us with the authority of our God."

Then some of the respected elders stood up and told the crowd, "Back when Hezekiah was king, a guy named Micah from Moresheth preached this to the people of Judah: 'This is a message from the God-of-the-Angel-Armies for you:'
"'Because of people like you, Zion's gonna be turned back into a farm, Jerusalem will be a pile of rocks, and the Temple mountain will just have a few scraggly trees.'
"Did King Hezekiah or anyone in Judah kill Micah of Moresheth for that sermon? No! Hezekiah respected him and begged God for mercy. And then God called off the disaster he had planned, right?
"Dudes, we are this close to bringing a massive disaster on ourselves."

(Sidenote: there was this other guy, Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-jearim, who had preached a similar message in God's name. He said the same stuff against the city and country, just like Jeremiah. When King Jehoiakim and his crew heard him, they decided to kill him. Uriah got scared and dipped to Egypt. But King Jehoiakim sent Elnathan son of Achbor with a squad to track him down. They dragged him back from Egypt, brought him to the king, and the king had him executed. They just dumped his body outside the city like it was nothing.
But for Jeremiah, a guy named Ahikam, son of Shaphan, stepped up and had his back, stopping the mob from straight-up lynching him.)

title: God's Ultimatum: Team Up with Babylon or Get Wrecked
paragraphs: So, way back when Zedekiah, Josiah's son, was the new king of Judah, God hit up Jeremiah with this message. He was like, 'Yo, make a harness and a yoke, and actually put it on yourself. Then, you gotta send a message to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre, and Sidon. Their reps are all in Jerusalem visiting King Zedekiah, so give them this message to take back to their bosses. It's from the God of Angel Armies, the God of Israel. Tell your masters this:

'Listen up. I'm the one who created the whole world—the earth, people, animals, everything. I did it all by myself, didn't need anyone's permission, and I can give it to whoever I want. And right now, I'm handing all these countries over to my servant Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon. I've even put the wild animals under his control. Every nation is gonna serve him, and then his son, and then his grandson. After that, his country's time is up, and the script will flip. Babylon will be the one serving. But until that day comes, any nation or kingdom that refuses to bow down to King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon and accept his rule will have to deal with me. I'll hit them with war, famine, and plagues until I've got them completely under his thumb.

'So don't even think about listening to your prophets, your spiritual gurus, or your fortune-tellers who are all saying they know what's up and telling you not to surrender to the king of Babylon. They're feeding you a bunch of straight-up lies, and if you fall for it, you'll end up exiled, miles away from home. I'll personally kick you out of your own land, and it'll be game over for you. But any nation that just accepts the rule of the king of Babylon and does what he says, I'll let that nation stay put and just mind its own business.'

Then I gave the same exact message to Zedekiah, the king of Judah. I said, 'You need to put on the yoke of the king of Babylon. Serve him and his people, and you'll get to live. Why would you choose to die in a war, or starve, or get some nasty disease? Because that's what God has promised will happen to any nation that doesn't side with Babylon. Stop listening to the prophets who are telling you not to submit to Babylon's king. They're lying to you, just preaching lies. God's official word on this is, 'I never sent those prophets, but they keep lying and claiming I did. If you listen to them, I'm gonna have to drive you out of here, and that'll be the end for all of you—you and your fake prophets.'

And finally, I talked to the priests and everyone else. I said, 'This is God's message: Stop listening to your prophets who keep telling you, 'Don't worry, the stuff that was stolen from God's Temple will be brought back from Babylon any day now.' That's a total lie. Don't listen to them. Just submit to the king of Babylon and live. Why would you do something that's gonna get this whole city wrecked and turned into a pile of rocks? If they were real prophets and actually had a message from God, they'd be praying to the God of Angel Armies that the stuff still left in the Temple, the king's palace, and Jerusalem doesn't also get hauled off to Babylon. Because here's the deal: the God of Angel Armies has already said that all the remaining Temple items—the pillars, the huge bronze basin, the stands, and all the other bowls and cups that King Nebuchadnezzar didn't grab when he exiled King Jehoiachin and the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem—he said all that stuff left behind will be taken to Babylon and will stay there until, as God says, 'I decide to deal with it and bring it all back where it belongs.''

title: Prophet vs. Prophet: The Ultimate Showdown
paragraphs: So, later that same year—it was the fifth month of King Zedekiah’s fourth year on the throne—this prophet named Hananiah, son of Azzur from Gibeon, rolled up on Jeremiah in God's Temple. He did this right in front of all the priests and everyone else who was there.

And Hananiah goes, “This message is straight from the God-of-the-Angel-Armies, the God of Israel: ‘I’m about to completely shatter the yoke of the king of Babylon. Before two years are up, I’m bringing back all the stuff from God’s Temple that King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon looted and dragged off to Babylon. I’m also bringing back Jehoiachin, son of Jehoiakim, the king of Judah, and all the exiles who got shipped off to Babylon.’ This is God's decree, for real. ‘Yep, I’m gonna break the king of Babylon’s yoke. You won’t be under his control anymore.’”

The prophet Jeremiah then stood up to the prophet Hananiah, right there in front of the priests and everyone in God’s Temple that day. Jeremiah said, “Awesome! I seriously hope that’s true—that God would actually back up your words by bringing the Temple stuff and all the exiles back from Babylon. But listen up, for real. Listen to what I’m about to say to you and all the people here: The prophets from way back, the ones before us, they always preached about judgment coming to big countries and kingdoms, warning about war, disaster, and plagues. So, any prophet who comes along preaching that everything’s great and there’s nothing to worry about is kinda sus. We’ll just have to wait and see. If what you say happens, then we’ll know for sure that God actually sent you.”

Right then, Hananiah snatched the yoke right off Jeremiah’s shoulders and smashed it to pieces. Then he announced to everyone, “This is God’s message: Just like this, I’m gonna smash the yoke of the king of Babylon and get him off the necks of all the nations—and it's gonna happen within two years.”
Jeremiah just walked away.

Later on, after Hananiah had smashed the yoke from his shoulders, Jeremiah got this message from God: “Go back and tell Hananiah, ‘This is God’s message: You smashed the wooden yoke bars, but now you’ve got iron ones. This is a message from the God-of-the-Angel-Armies, Israel’s own God: I’ve put an iron yoke on all these nations. They are now stuck serving Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. They’ll do whatever he says. I’m even putting him in charge of the wild animals.’”

So, the prophet Jeremiah told the prophet Hananiah, “Hold up, Hananiah! God never sent you. You’ve got this whole country believing a bunch of lies! And because of that, God says, ‘You say you were sent? Oh, I’ll send you somewhere, alright—straight off the face of the earth! Before this year is over, you’ll be dead, because you started a rebellion against God.’”
And the prophet Hananiah died that exact same year, in the seventh month.

title: God's Long-Game Plan vs. Fake Prophets
paragraphs: This is the letter that Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem to the elders, priests, prophets, and all the other people Nebuchadnezzar had deported from Jerusalem to Babylon. This was after King Jehoiachin, the queen mother, the government officials, and all the skilled workers had been taken away.
The letter was delivered by Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, who were sent to King Nebuchadnezzar in Babylon by King Zedekiah of Judah. Here's what the letter said:
This is a message from the God of Angel Armies, the God of Israel, to all the people I sent from Jerusalem to Babylon:
"Build houses and settle down. Plant gardens and eat what you grow.
Get married and have kids. Make sure your kids get married and have kids, too, so you grow into a community there and don't just fade away.
Get invested in the city where you are. Work for its good, and pray for it. When it does well, you'll do well."

Yeah, for real, this is a message from the God of Angel Armies, the God of Israel: "Don't let these so-called prophets and spiritual gurus who are everywhere fool you with their lies. Don't listen to their made-up dreams they're spinning to keep you happy. They're a bunch of liars preaching lies and claiming I sent them. I never sent them, for real." That's God's decree.

Here's God's word on it: "When Babylon's seventy years are up, and not a day sooner, I'll come through for you. I'll keep my promise and bring you back home. I know what I'm doing. I have it all planned out—plans to take care of you, not to abandon you. Plans to give you the future you're hoping for.
"When you call out to me, when you come and pray to me, I'll be listening.
"When you start looking for me, you'll find me.
"Seriously, when you're all in, wanting to find me more than anything, I'll make sure you're not disappointed." God's decree.
"I'll turn things around for you. I'll bring you back from all the countries where I scattered you," says God, "and bring you home to the place I sent you from. You can count on it.

"But for now, you're all hyped about these new prophets who call themselves 'Babylon specialists,' saying 'God sent them just for us!' Well, God's setting the record straight: The king still on David's throne and all the people left in Jerusalem who weren't exiled with you? They're in for some rough times. The God of Angel Armies says, 'Watch out! A total disaster is coming: war, famine, and disease! They're like a barrel of rotten fruit. I'm going to clear them out of the land with war, famine, and disease. The whole world will be disgusted by the sight and smell. They'll end up in the worst places because they wouldn't listen to a single thing I said when I sent my prophets to them over and over. Nope, they wouldn't listen to a word.'" That's God's decree.

"And you exiles I sent from Jerusalem to Babylon—listen to God's message. Regarding Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, those 'Babylon specialists' who are preaching lies in my name: I'm handing them over to King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, and he's going to execute them right in front of you. The other exiles from Judah will even turn it into a curse: 'May God roast you like the king of Babylon roasted Zedekiah and Ahab in the fire!' Those two guys, who were sexual predators and fake prophets, got what was coming to them. They were sleeping with their neighbors' wives and preaching lies in my name. I never sent them. I had nothing to do with them." God's decree.
"They won't get away with anything. I saw it all."

And this is the message for Shemaiah the Nehelamite: "The God of Angel Armies, the God of Israel, says: You went and sent letters on your own to all the people in Jerusalem, to the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, and to the other priests. In your letter, you told Zephaniah that God made him the priest in charge of the Temple, replacing Jehoiada, and that it's his job to lock up any crazy person who claims to be a prophet.

"So why haven't you shut down Jeremiah of Anathoth, who's going around acting like a prophet? He even had the nerve to write to us in Babylon, saying, 'It's going to be a long time, so build houses, settle down, plant gardens, and start cooking with local ingredients.'"
The priest Zephaniah read that letter to the prophet Jeremiah.

Then God told Jeremiah, "Send this message to all the exiles. Tell them what God says about Shemaiah the Nehelamite: Shemaiah is preaching lies to you. I didn't send him. He's tricking you into believing lies. So here's God's verdict: I'm going to punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his entire family. He'll have no one left. No one from his family will be around to see the good things I'm going to do for my people, because he preached rebellion against me." That's God's decree.

title: God's Epic Comeback Plan
paragraphs: So, this is the message Jeremiah got straight from God. God, the God of Israel, was like, "Yo, write down everything I'm telling you. Seriously, a time is coming when I'm gonna turn things around for my people, Israel and Judah. I, God, am saying it. I'll bring them back to the land I gave their ancestors, and they'll own it again."
This is how God explained it to Israel and Judah:
God's message was this:

"You can hear the cries of panic. The peace is totally gone. Ask around, look for yourself! Can guys have babies? So why do I see all these tough dudes holding their stomachs like they're in labor, their faces all twisted and pale? It's the darkest day ever, no day has ever been like it. It's a time of major trouble for Jacob's descendants—but they'll get through it.
"And then I'll step in. I'll break the yoke off their necks and cut them free. No more being slaves to foreigners! They'll serve their God and the king from David's line that I'll set up for them.

"So don't be scared, my servant Jacob. Don't lose hope, Israel. Look, I'm going to save you from those faraway places and bring your kids back from exile. Jacob's people will come back and have a good, safe life. I'll be with you. I'll save you. I'll destroy all the nations where I scattered you, but I won't destroy you. I'll discipline you, but fairly. I won't let you get away with just a slap on the wrist."
This is God's message:

"You're basically a lost cause, as good as dead. Everyone has given up on you. You're hopeless. All your so-called friends have bailed on you without a second thought. But I'm the one who delivered the final blow, a punishment you won't forget, because your guilt was huge and your sins were endless. So why are you feeling sorry for yourself and licking your wounds? You deserved all of this, and more. Because your guilt was so massive and your sins were never-ending, I did all this to you.

"But everyone who hurt you will get hurt; your enemies will become slaves. The people who robbed you will be robbed; those who looted you will become loot. As for you, I'll bring healing and cure what seemed incurable, because everyone gave up on you and called you a hopeless case—that good-for-nothing Zion."
Again, God's message:

"I'm going to turn things around for Jacob's descendants. I'll have compassion and rebuild their homes. The city will be rebuilt on its old foundations, and the mansions will be amazing again. You'll hear thanksgiving from the windows and laughter from the doors. Things will keep getting better. The depressing days are over. They'll thrive and flourish. The days of being looked down on will be over. They'll look forward to having kids again and being a community I'm proud of. I'll punish anyone who hurts them, and their prince will be one of their own. Their leader will come from their own people. I'll give him easy access to me. Who would dare to approach me uninvited?" God declares.
"And that's the deal: You'll be my very own people, and I'll be your very own God."

Watch out! God's hurricane is coming, a powerful blast, and it will spin the heads of the wicked like a tornado! God's intense anger won't stop until he has finished the job he started. When it's all done, you'll see it was the right thing to do.

title: God's Epic Comeback Plan for Israel
paragraphs: Yo, when this all goes down—God's dropping this decree—it's gonna be crystal clear: I'll be the God for every single person in Israel, and for real, they'll be my people.
Here's how God put it:

"The people who survived the craziness found grace in the desert. Israel was out there looking for a place to rest, and they ran right into me, looking for them!" God told them, "I have never stopped loving you and I never will. Expect love, and then more love! So now I'm gonna start over with you and build you up again, dear Israel. You'll get back to singing, grabbing tambourines, and joining the dance. You'll go back to your work, planting vineyards on the Samaritan hills, and you'll get to sit back and enjoy the fruit—you'll love that harvest. The time is coming when watchmen on the hills of Ephraim will shout, 'Let's go! Time to head to Zion and meet our God!'"
Oh yeah, God says so:
"Shout for joy at the top of your lungs for Jacob! Tell the number-one nation the good news! Get loud! Sing praises. Say, 'God has saved his people, the core of Israel.'
"Watch what's next:
"I'm bringing my people back from the north and gathering them from the ends of the earth. I'm getting the blind, the lame, pregnant women, and even new moms—bringing them all back, a huge crowd!
"Watch them come! They'll be crying tears of joy as I lead them by the hand to fresh, flowing streams, on smooth, easy paths. Why? Because I'm Israel's Father, and Ephraim is my firstborn son.

"Listen up, nations! This is God's Message! Spread it all over the world! Tell them, 'The One who scattered Israel will gather them back together. From now on, he'll watch over them like a shepherd with his flock.' I, God, will pay a huge price to get Jacob back; I'll rescue him from that big bully, Babylon. The people will climb Mount Zion shouting with joy, their faces glowing because of God's blessings—grain, wine, oil, and tons of sheep and cattle. Their lives will be like a well-watered garden, never drying up again. Young women will dance and be happy, and the young and old men will join in. I'll turn their crying into laughing, comforting them and swapping their grief for joy. I'll make sure their priests have plenty to eat and my people have more than enough." That's God's decree.
Again, God's Message:

"Listen! You can hear wailing coming from Ramah, wild and bitter crying. It's Rachel weeping for her children, and she won't be comforted. Her children are gone—exiled far away." But God says, "Stop all the crying, hold back your tears. Your hard work of grieving will pay off." God's decree. "They're coming home! There's hope for your kids." God's decree.

"I've heard Ephraim's regret. I heard it loud and clear. He's saying, 'You really trained me. You broke me like a wild horse. Now that I'm trained and obedient, put me to work. You are my God. After all those years of doing my own thing, I'm sorry. After you taught me to obey, I was so ashamed of my wild past. I was so humiliated, I could only beat my chest. Will I ever live this down?'

"Oh! Ephraim is my dear, dear son, the child I love so much! Every time I even mention him, my heart just longs for him! Everything in me cries out for him. I'm waiting for him with open arms." God's decree.

"Put up signs to mark your way home. Get a good map. Check out the road conditions. The way you left is the way you'll come back. Come back, dear Israel, come back to your hometowns. How long are you going to be so indecisive? When are you going to make up your mind? God is going to do something brand new in this land: a changed woman will embrace the God who changes her!"

A Message from the God of Angel Armies, Israel's God: "When I've turned everything around and brought my people back, you'll hear the old sayings on the streets again: 'God bless you!'... 'O True Home!'... 'O Holy Mountain!' All the people of Judah, whether they live in the city or the country, will get along great.
I'll refresh the tired, and I'll restore the weary.
Just then I woke up and looked around—man, that was a good sleep!

"Get ready. The time is coming"—God's decree—"when I will plant people and animals in Israel and Judah, just like a farmer plants seeds. And just like I was relentless before in pulling up, tearing down, and destroying, now I'm sticking with them to build and plant as they start over.
"When that time comes, you won't hear that old saying anymore,
'The parents ate sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge.'
"Nope, everyone will be responsible for their own sin. If you eat the sour grapes, you're the one who gets the stomachache.

"That's right. The time is coming when I will make a brand-new covenant with Israel and Judah. It won't be like the covenant I made with their ancestors when I led them out of Egypt. They broke that one, even though I was their Master." God's decree.

"This is the new covenant I'll make with Israel when the time comes. I will put my law inside them—write it on their hearts!—and I will be their God, and they will be my people. They won't have to teach each other about God anymore. They'll all know me personally, from the least to the greatest. I'll wipe the slate clean for every one of them. I'll forget they ever sinned!" God's decree.
God's Message, from the God who gives the sun to light the day and the moon and stars to brighten the night, who stirs up the ocean into a foamy rage, whose name is the God of Angel Armies:
"If this whole ordered universe ever fell apart into chaos before me"—God's decree—"Then and only then would Israel fall apart and stop being a nation before me."
God's Message:
"If the skies could be measured and the foundations of the earth explored, then and only then would I turn my back on Israel because of all they've done." God's decree.

"The time is coming"—it's God's decree—"when God's city will be rebuilt, all the way from the Citadel of Hanamel to the Corner Gate. The master plan will go west to Gareb Hill and then around to Goath. The whole valley to the south where they dump ashes and bodies—a real death valley!—and all the fields out to the Kidron Brook on the east, as far as the Horse Gate, will be a holy place, consecrated to me.
"This city will never again be torn down or destroyed."
